#### Level 1: Martial Arts {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level1MartialArts}

Your practice of martial arts gives you mastery of combat styles that use your [**Unarmed Strike**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:unarmedstrike "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#unarmedstrike") and Monk weapons, which are the following:

- Simple Melee weapons
- Martial Melee weapons that have the [**Light**](#phb-2024:equipment:light "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/equipment#light") property

You gain the following benefits while you are unarmed or wielding only Monk weapons and you aren’t wearing armor or wielding a Shield.

**_Bonus Unarmed Strike._** You can make an [**Unarmed Strike**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:unarmedstrike "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#unarmedstrike") as a Bonus Action.

**_Martial Arts Die._** You can roll 1d6 in place of the normal damage of your [**Unarmed Strike**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:unarmedstrike "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#unarmedstrike") or Monk weapons. This die changes as you gain Monk levels, as shown in the Martial Arts column of the Monk Features table.

**_Dexterous Attacks._** You can use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls of your [**Unarmed Strikes**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:unarmedstrike "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#unarmedstrike") and Monk weapons. In addition, when you use the Grapple or Shove option of your Unarmed Strike, you can use your Dexterity modifier instead of your Strength modifier to determine the save DC.

#### Level 1: Unarmored Defense {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level1UnarmoredDefense}

While you aren’t wearing armor or wielding a Shield, your base [**Armor Class**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:armorclass "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#armorclass") equals 10 plus your Dexterity and Wisdom modifiers.

#### Level 2: Monk’s Focus {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level2MonksFocus}

Your focus and martial training allow you to harness a well of extraordinary energy within yourself. This energy is represented by Focus Points. Your Monk level determines the number of points you have, as shown in the Focus Points column of the [Monk Features table](#phb-2024:character-classes:monkfeatures "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#monkfeatures").

You can expend these points to enhance or fuel certain Monk features. You start knowing three such features: Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind, each of which is detailed below.

When you expend a Focus Point, it is unavailable until you finish a [**Short**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:shortrest "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#shortrest") or [**Long Rest**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:longrest "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#longrest"), at the end of which you regain all your expended points.

Some features that use Focus Points require your target to make a saving throw. The save DC equals 8 plus your Wisdom modifier and Proficiency Bonus.

**_Flurry of Blows._** You can expend 1 Focus Point to make two [**Unarmed Strikes**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:unarmedstrike "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#unarmedstrike") as a Bonus Action.

**_Patient Defense._** You can take the [**Disengage**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:disengageaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#disengageaction") action as a Bonus Action. Alternatively, you can expend 1 Focus Point to take both the [**Disengage**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:disengageaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#disengageaction") and the [**Dodge**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:dodgeaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#dodgeaction") actions as a Bonus Action.

**_Step of the Wind._** You can take the [**Dash**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:dashaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#dashaction") action as a Bonus Action. Alternatively, you can expend 1 Focus Point to take both the [**Disengage**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:disengageaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#disengageaction") and [**Dash**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:dashaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#dashaction") actions as a Bonus Action, and your jump distance is doubled for the turn.

#### Level 2: Unarmored Movement {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level2UnarmoredMovement}

Your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren’t wearing armor or wielding a Shield. This bonus increases when you reach certain Monk levels, as shown on the [Monk Features table](#phb-2024:character-classes:monkfeatures "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#monkfeatures").

#### Level 2: Uncanny Metabolism {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level2UncannyMetabolism}

When you roll [**Initiative**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:initiative "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#initiative"), you can regain all expended Focus Points. When you do so, roll your Martial Arts die, and regain a number of Hit Points equal to your Monk level plus the number rolled.

Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a [**Long Rest**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:longrest "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#longrest").

#### Level 3: Deflect Attacks {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level3DeflectAttacks}

When an attack roll hits you and its damage includes Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, you can take a Reaction to reduce the attack’s total damage against you. The reduction equals 1d10 plus your Dexterity modifier and Monk level.

If you reduce the damage to 0, you can expend 1 Focus Point to redirect some of the attack’s force. If you do so, choose a creature you can see within 5 feet of yourself if the attack was a melee attack or a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself that isn’t behind [**Total Cover**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:cover "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#cover") if the attack was a ranged attack. That creature must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take damage equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die plus your Dexterity modifier. The damage is the same type dealt by the attack.

#### Level 3: Monk Subclass {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level3MonkSubclass}

You gain a Monk subclass of your choice. The [Warrior of Mercy](#phb-2024:character-classes:warriorofmercy "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#warriorofmercy"), [Warrior of Shadow](#phb-2024:character-classes:warriorofshadow "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#warriorofshadow"), [Warrior of the Elements](#phb-2024:character-classes:warrioroftheelements "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#warrioroftheelements"), and [Warrior of the Open Hand](#phb-2024:character-classes:warrioroftheopenhand "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#warrioroftheopenhand") subclasses are detailed after this class’s description. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Monk levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass’s features that are of your Monk level or lower.

#### Level 4: Ability Score Improvement {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level4AbilityScoreImprovement}

You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see [chapter 5](#phb-2024:feats:abilityscoreimprovement "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/feats#abilityscoreimprovement")) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Monk levels 8, 12, and 16.

#### Level 4: Slow Fall {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level4SlowFall}

You can take a Reaction when you fall to reduce any damage you take from the fall by an amount equal to five times your Monk level.

#### Level 5: Extra Attack {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level5ExtraAttack}

You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the [**Attack**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:attackaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#attackaction") action on your turn.

#### Level 5: Stunning Strike {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level5StunningStrike}

Once per turn when you hit a creature with a Monk weapon or an [**Unarmed Strike**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:unarmedstrike "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#unarmedstrike"), you can expend 1 Focus Point to attempt a stunning strike. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target has the [**Stunned**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:stunnedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#stunnedcondition") condition until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, the target’s Speed is halved until the start of your next turn, and the next attack roll made against the target before then has [**Advantage**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:advantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#advantage").

#### Level 6: Empowered Strikes {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level6EmpoweredStrikes}

Whenever you deal damage with your [**Unarmed Strike**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:unarmedstrike "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#unarmedstrike"), it can deal your choice of Force damage or its normal damage type.

#### Level 7: Evasion {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level7Evasion}

When you’re subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail.

You don’t benefit from this feature if you have the [**Incapacitated**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:incapacitatedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition") condition.

#### Level 9: Acrobatic Movement {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level9AcrobaticMovement}

While you aren’t wearing armor or wielding a Shield, you gain the ability to move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling during the movement.

#### Level 10: Heightened Focus {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level10HeightenedFocus}

Your Flurry of Blows, Patient Defense, and Step of the Wind gain the following benefits.

**_Flurry of Blows._** You can expend 1 Focus Point to use Flurry of Blows and make three [**Unarmed Strikes**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:unarmedstrike "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#unarmedstrike") with it instead of two.

**_Patient Defense._** When you expend a Focus Point to use Patient Defense, you gain a number of [**Temporary Hit Points**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:temporaryhitpoints "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#temporaryhitpoints") equal to two rolls of your Martial Arts die.

**_Step of the Wind._** When you expend a Focus Point to use Step of the Wind, you can choose a willing creature within 5 feet of yourself that is Large or smaller. You move the creature with you until the end of your turn. The creature’s movement doesn’t provoke [**Opportunity Attacks**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:opportunityattack "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#opportunityattack").

#### Level 10: Self-Restoration {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level10SelfRestoration}

Through sheer force of will, you can remove one of the following conditions from yourself at the end of each of your turns: [**Charmed**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:charmedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#charmedcondition"), [**Frightened**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:frightenedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition"), or [**Poisoned**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:poisonedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#poisonedcondition").

In addition, forgoing food and drink doesn’t give you levels of [**Exhaustion**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:exhaustioncondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#exhaustioncondition").

#### Level 13: Deflect Energy {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level13DeflectEnergy}

You can now use your Deflect Attacks feature against attacks that deal any damage type, not just Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing.

#### Level 14: Disciplined Survivor {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level14DisciplinedSurvivor}

Your physical and mental discipline grant you proficiency in all saving throws.

Additionally, whenever you make a saving throw and fail, you can expend 1 Focus Point to reroll it, and you must use the new roll.

#### Level 15: Perfect Focus {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level15PerfectFocus}

When you roll [**Initiative**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:initiative "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#initiative") and don’t use Uncanny Metabolism, you regain expended Focus Points until you have 4 if you have 3 or fewer.

#### Level 18: Superior Defense {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level18SuperiorDefense}

At the start of your turn, you can expend 3 Focus Points to bolster yourself against harm for 1 minute or until you have the [**Incapacitated**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:incapacitatedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition") condition. During that time, you have Resistance to all damage except Force damage.

#### Level 19: Epic Boon {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level19EpicBoon}

You gain an Epic Boon feat (see [chapter 5](#phb-2024:feats:EpicBoonFeats "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/feats#EpicBoonFeats")) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. [Boon of Irresistible Offense](#phb-2024:feats:boonofirresistibleoffense "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/feats#boonofirresistibleoffense") is recommended.

#### Level 20: Body and Mind {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level20BodyandMind}

You have developed your body and mind to new heights. Your Dexterity and Wisdom scores increase by 4, to a maximum of 25.

### Monk Subclasses {#phb-2024:character-classes:MonkSubclasses}

A Monk subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Monk levels, as specified in the subclass. This section presents the [Warrior of Mercy](#phb-2024:character-classes:warriorofmercy "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#warriorofmercy"), [Warrior of Shadow](#phb-2024:character-classes:warriorofshadow "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#warriorofshadow"), [Warrior of the Elements](#phb-2024:character-classes:warrioroftheelements "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#warrioroftheelements"), and [Warrior of the Open Hand](#phb-2024:character-classes:warrioroftheopenhand "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#warrioroftheopenhand") subclasses.

#### Warrior of Mercy {#phb-2024:character-classes:WarriorofMercy}

_Manipulate Forces of Life and Death_

Warriors of Mercy manipulate the life force of others. These Monks are wandering physicians, but they bring a swift end to their enemies. They often wear masks, presenting themselves as faceless bringers of life and death.

[![Warrior of Mercy Subclass (Artist: OLIVIER BERNARD)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/03-046.warrior-of-mercy.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/03-046.warrior-of-mercy.png)

##### Level 3: Hand of Harm {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level3HandofHarm}

Once per turn when you hit a creature with an [**Unarmed Strike**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:unarmedstrike "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#unarmedstrike") and deal damage, you can expend 1 Focus Point to deal extra Necrotic damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die plus your Wisdom modifier.

##### Level 3: Hand of Healing {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level3HandofHealing}

As a [**Magic**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:magicaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#magicaction") action, you can expend 1 Focus Point to touch a creature and restore a number of Hit Points equal to a roll of your Martial Arts die plus your Wisdom modifier.

When you use your Flurry of Blows, you can replace one of the [**Unarmed Strikes**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:unarmedstrike "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#unarmedstrike") with a use of this feature without expending a Focus Point for the healing.

##### Level 3: Implements of Mercy {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level3ImplementsofMercy}

You gain proficiency in the [**Insight**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills") and [**Medicine**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills") skills and proficiency with the Herbalism Kit.

##### Level 6: Physician’s Touch {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level6PhysiciansTouch}

Your Hand of Harm and Hand of Healing improve, as detailed below.

**_Hand of Harm._** When you use Hand of Harm on a creature, you can also give that creature the [**Poisoned**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:poisonedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#poisonedcondition") condition until the end of your next turn.

**_Hand of Healing._** When you use Hand of Healing, you can also end one of the following conditions on the creature you heal: [**Blinded**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:blindedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#blindedcondition"), [**Deafened**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:deafenedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#deafenedcondition"), [**Paralyzed**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:paralyzedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#paralyzedcondition"), [**Poisoned**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:poisonedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#poisonedcondition"), or [**Stunned**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:stunnedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#stunnedcondition").

##### Level 11: Flurry of Healing and Harm {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level11FlurryofHealingandHarm}

When you use Flurry of Blows, you can replace each of the [**Unarmed Strikes**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:unarmedstrike "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#unarmedstrike") with a use of Hand of Healing without expending Focus Points for the healing.

In addition, when you make an Unarmed Strike with Flurry of Blows and deal damage, you can use Hand of Harm with that strike without expending a Focus Point for Hand of Harm. You can still use Hand of Harm only once per turn.

You can use these benefits a total number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a [**Long Rest**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:longrest "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#longrest").

##### Level 17: Hand of Ultimate Mercy {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level17HandofUltimateMercy}

Your mastery of life energy opens the door to the ultimate mercy. As a [**Magic**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:magicaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#magicaction") action, you can touch the corpse of a creature that died within the past 24 hours and expend 5 Focus Points. The creature then returns to life with a number of Hit Points equal to 4d10 plus your Wisdom modifier. If the creature died with any of the following conditions, the creature revives with the conditions removed: [**Blinded**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:blindedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#blindedcondition"), [**Deafened**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:deafenedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#deafenedcondition"), [**Paralyzed**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:paralyzedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#paralyzedcondition"), [**Poisoned**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:poisonedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#poisonedcondition"), and [**Stunned**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:stunnedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#stunnedcondition").

Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a [**Long Rest**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:longrest "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#longrest").

#### Warrior of Shadow {#phb-2024:character-classes:WarriorofShadow}

[![Warrior of Shadow Subclass (Artist: NATHANIEL HIMAWAN)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/03-047.warrior-of-shadow.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/03-047.warrior-of-shadow.png)

_Harness Shadow Power for Stealth and Subterfuge_

Warriors of Shadow practice stealth and subterfuge, harnessing the power of the Shadowfell. They are at home in darkness, able to draw gloom around themselves to hide, leap from shadow to shadow, and take on a wraithlike form.

##### Level 3: Shadow Arts {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level3ShadowArts}

You have learned to draw on the power of the Shadowfell, gaining the following benefits.

**_Darkness._** You can expend 1 Focus Point to cast the [**Darkness**](#ref:spell:2619080-darkness "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619080-darkness") spell without spell components. You can see within the spell’s area when you cast it with this feature. While the spell persists, you can move its area of [**Darkness**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:darkness "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#darkness") to a space within 60 feet of yourself at the start of each of your turns.

**_Darkvision._** You gain [**Darkvision**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:darkvision "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#darkvision") with a range of 60 feet. If you already have Darkvision, its range increases by 60 feet.

**_Shadowy Figments._** You know the [**Minor Illusion**](#ref:spell:2619039-minor-illusion "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619039-minor-illusion") spell. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for it.

##### Level 6: Shadow Step {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level6ShadowStep}

While entirely within [**Dim Light**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:dimlight "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#dimlight") or [**Darkness**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:darkness "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#darkness"), you can use a Bonus Action to teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is also in Dim Light or Darkness. You then have [**Advantage**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:advantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#advantage") on the next melee attack you make before the end of the current turn.

##### Level 11: Improved Shadow Step {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level11ImprovedShadowStep}

You can draw on your Shadowfell connection to empower your teleportation. When you use your Shadow Step, you can expend 1 Focus Point to remove the requirement that you must start and end in [**Dim Light**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:dimlight "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#dimlight") or [**Darkness**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:darkness "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#darkness") for that use of the feature. As part of this Bonus Action, you can make an [**Unarmed Strike**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:unarmedstrike "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#unarmedstrike") immediately after you teleport.

##### Level 17: Cloak of Shadows {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level17CloakofShadows}

As a [**Magic**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:magicaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#magicaction") action while entirely within [**Dim Light**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:dimlight "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#dimlight") or [**Darkness**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:darkness "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#darkness"), you can expend 3 Focus Points to shroud yourself with shadows for 1 minute, until you have the [**Incapacitated**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:incapacitatedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition") condition, or until you end your turn in [**Bright Light**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:brightlight "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#brightlight"). While shrouded by these shadows, you gain the following benefits.

**_Invisibility._** You have the [**Invisible**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:invisiblecondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#invisiblecondition") condition.

**_Partially Incorporeal._** You can move through occupied spaces as if they were [**Difficult Terrain**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:difficultterrain "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#difficultterrain"). If you end your turn in such a space, you are shunted to the last unoccupied space you were in.

**_Shadow Flurry._** You can use your Flurry of Blows without expending any Focus Points.

#### Warrior of the Elements {#phb-2024:character-classes:WarrioroftheElements}

_Wield Strikes and Bursts of Elemental Power_

Warriors of the Elements tap into the power of the Elemental Planes. Harnessing their supernatural focus, these Monks momentarily tame the energy of the Elemental Chaos to empower themselves in and out of battle.

[![Warrior of the Elements Subclass (Artist: KATERINA LADON)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/03-048.warrior-of-the-elements.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/03-048.warrior-of-the-elements.png)

##### Level 3: Elemental Attunement {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level3ElementalAttunement}

At the start of your turn, you can expend 1 Focus Point to imbue yourself with elemental energy. The energy lasts for 10 minutes or until you have the [**Incapacitated**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:incapacitatedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition") condition. You gain the following benefits while this feature is active.

**_Reach._** When you make an [**Unarmed Strike**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:unarmedstrike "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#unarmedstrike"), your reach is 10 feet greater than normal, as elemental energy extends from you.

**_Elemental Strikes._** Whenever you hit with your [**Unarmed Strike**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:unarmedstrike "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#unarmedstrike"), you can cause it to deal your choice of Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage rather than its normal damage type. When you deal one of these types with it, you can also force the target to make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, you can move the target up to 10 feet toward or away from you, as elemental energy swirls around it.

##### Level 3: Manipulate Elements {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level3ManipulateElements}

You know the [**Elementalism**](#ref:spell:2618834-elementalism "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618834-elementalism") spell. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for it.

##### Level 6: Elemental Burst {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level6ElementalBurst}

As a [**Magic**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:magicaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#magicaction") action, you can expend 2 Focus Points to cause elemental energy to burst in a 20-foot-radius [**Sphere**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:sphereareaofeffect "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#sphereareaofeffect") centered on a point within 120 feet of yourself. Choose a damage type: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder.

Each creature in the Sphere must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes damage of the chosen type equal to three rolls of your Martial Arts die. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage.

##### Level 11: Stride of the Elements {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level11StrideoftheElements}

While your Elemental Attunement is active, you also have a Fly Speed and a Swim Speed equal to your Speed.

##### Level 17: Elemental Epitome {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level17ElementalEpitome}

While your Elemental Attunement is active, you also gain the following benefits.

**_Damage Resistance._** You gain Resistance to one of the following damage types of your choice: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder. At the start of each of your turns, you can change this choice.

**_Destructive Stride._** When you use your Step of the Wind, your Speed increases by 20 feet until the end of the turn. For that duration, any creature of your choice takes damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die when you enter a space within 5 feet of it. The damage type is your choice of Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder. A creature can take this damage only once per turn.

**_Empowered Strikes._** Once on each of your turns, you can deal extra damage to a target equal to one roll of your Martial Arts die when you hit it with an [**Unarmed Strike**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:unarmedstrike "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#unarmedstrike"). The extra damage is the same type dealt by that strike.

#### Warrior of the Open Hand {#phb-2024:character-classes:WarrioroftheOpenHand}

[![Warrior of the Open Hand Subclass (Artist: KATERINA LADON)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/03-049.warrior-of-the-open-hand.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/03-049.warrior-of-the-open-hand.png)

_Master Unarmed Combat Techniques_

Warriors of the Open Hand are masters of unarmed combat. They learn techniques to push and trip their opponents and manipulate their own energy to protect themselves from harm.

##### Level 3: Open Hand Technique {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level3OpenHandTechnique}

Whenever you hit a creature with an attack granted by your Flurry of Blows, you can impose one of the following effects on that target.

**_Addle._** The target can’t make [**Opportunity Attacks**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:opportunityattack "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#opportunityattack") until the start of its next turn.

**_Push._** The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed up to 15 feet away from you.

**_Topple._** The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or have the [**Prone**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:pronecondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#pronecondition") condition.

##### Level 6: Wholeness of Body {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level6WholenessofBody}

You gain the ability to heal yourself. As a Bonus Action, you can roll your Martial Arts die. You regain a number of Hit Points equal to the number rolled plus your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1 Hit Point regained).

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a [**Long Rest**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:longrest "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#longrest").

##### Level 11: Fleet Step {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level11FleetStep}

When you take a Bonus Action other than Step of the Wind, you can also use Step of the Wind immediately after that Bonus Action.

##### Level 17: Quivering Palm {#phb-2024:character-classes:Level17QuiveringPalm}

You gain the ability to set up lethal vibrations in someone’s body. When you hit a creature with an [**Unarmed Strike**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:unarmedstrike "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#unarmedstrike"), you can expend 4 Focus Points to start these imperceptible vibrations, which last for a number of days equal to your Monk level. The vibrations are harmless unless you take an action to end them. Alternatively, when you take the [**Attack**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:attackaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#attackaction") action on your turn, you can forgo one of the attacks to end the vibrations. To end them, you and the target must be on the same plane of existence. When you end them, the target must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 10d12 Force damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

You can have only one creature under the effect of this feature at a time. You can end the vibrations harmlessly (no action required).

</CHAPTER>

<CHAPTER id="phb-2024:character-classes-continued" title="Character Classes Continued">

# Chapter 3: Character Classes (Continued) {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:Chapter3CharacterClassesContinued}

Character class provides a character’s most exciting capabilities. This chapter offers twelve classes, each of which contains four subclasses—all summarized below.

[![Image](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/03-002.barbarian-symbol.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/03-002.barbarian-symbol.png)

_**Barbarian.**_ Storm with Rage, and wade into hand-to-hand combat. Then follow the Path of the...

_[Berserker](#phb-2024:character-classes:pathoftheberserker "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#pathoftheberserker")_ to unleash raw violence.

_[Wild Heart](#phb-2024:character-classes:pathofthewildheart "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#pathofthewildheart")_ to manifest kinship with animals.

_[World Tree](#phb-2024:character-classes:pathoftheworldtree "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#pathoftheworldtree")_ to tap into cosmic vitality.

_[Zealot](#phb-2024:character-classes:pathofthezealot "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#pathofthezealot")_ to rage in union with a god.

---

[![Image](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/03-003.bard-symbol.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/03-003.bard-symbol.png)

_**Bard.**_ Perform spells that inspire and heal allies or beguile foes. Then join the College of...

_[Dance](#phb-2024:character-classes:collegeofdance "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#collegeofdance")_ to harness agility in battle.

_[Glamour](#phb-2024:character-classes:collegeofglamour "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#collegeofglamour")_ to weave beguiling Feywild magic.

_[Lore](#phb-2024:character-classes:collegeoflore "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#collegeoflore")_ to collect knowledge and magical secrets.

_[Valor](#phb-2024:character-classes:collegeofvalor "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#collegeofvalor")_ to wield weapons with spells.

---

[![Image](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/03-004.cleric-symbol.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/03-004.cleric-symbol.png)

_**Cleric.**_ Invoke divine magic to heal, bolster, and smite. Then harness the...

_[Life Domain](#phb-2024:character-classes:lifedomain "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#lifedomain")_ to be a master of healing.

_[Light Domain](#phb-2024:character-classes:lightdomain "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#lightdomain")_ to wield searing, warding light.

_[Trickery Domain](#phb-2024:character-classes:trickerydomain "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#trickerydomain")_ to bedevil foes with mischief.

_[War Domain](#phb-2024:character-classes:wardomain "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#wardomain")_ to inspire valor and chastise foes.

---

[![Image](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/03-005.druid-symbol.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/03-005.druid-symbol.png)

_**Druid.**_ Channel nature magic to heal, shape-shift, and control the elements. Then join the Circle of the...

_[Land](#phb-2024:character-classes:circleoftheland "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#circleoftheland")_ to draw on the magic of the environment.

_[Moon](#phb-2024:character-classes:circleofthemoon "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#circleofthemoon")_ to adopt powerful animal forms.

_[Sea](#phb-2024:character-classes:circleofthesea "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#circleofthesea")_ to channel tides and storms.

_[Stars](#phb-2024:character-classes:circleofthestars "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#circleofthestars")_ to gain powers in a starry form.

---

[![Image](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/03-006.fighter-symbol.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/03-006.fighter-symbol.png)

_**Fighter.**_ Master all weapons and armor. Then embody the...

_[Battle Master](#phb-2024:character-classes:battlemaster "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#battlemaster")_ to use special combat maneuvers.

_[Champion](#phb-2024:character-classes:champion "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#champion")_ to strive for peak combat prowess.

## Paladin {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:Paladin}

[![A Devout Warrior of Sacred Oaths (Artist: MICHAEL BROUSSARD)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/04-001.paladin.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/04-001.paladin.png)

**Core Paladin Traits**

| Primary Ability            | Strength and Charisma                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Hit Point Die              | D10 per Paladin level                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Saving Throw Proficiencies | Wisdom and Charisma                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Skill Proficiencies        | _Choose 2:_ [**Athletics**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills"), [**Insight**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills"), [**Intimidation**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills"), [**Medicine**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills"), [**Persuasion**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills"), or [**Religion**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills")                                                                         |
| Weapon Proficiencies       | Simple and Martial weapons                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Armor Training             | Light, Medium, and Heavy armor and Shields                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Starting Equipment         | _Choose A or B:_ (A) [**Chain Mail**](#ref:equipment:16-chain-mail "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/16-chain-mail"), [**Shield**](#ref:equipment:8-shield "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/8-shield"), [**Longsword**](#ref:equipment:4-longsword "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/4-longsword"), 6 [**Javelins**](#ref:equipment:8-javelin "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/8-javelin"), [**Holy Symbol**](#ref:equipment:514-holy-symbol "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/514-holy-symbol"), [**Priest’s Pack**](#ref:equipment:405-priests-pack "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/405-priests-pack"), and 9 GP; or (B) 150 GP |

Paladins are united by their oaths to stand against the forces of annihilation and corruption. Whether sworn before a god’s altar, in a sacred glade before nature spirits, or in a moment of desperation and grief with the dead as the only witnesses, a Paladin’s oath is a powerful bond. It is a source of power that turns a devout warrior into a blessed champion.

Paladins train to learn the skills of combat, mastering a variety of weapons and armor. Even so, their martial skills are secondary to the magical power they wield: power to heal the injured, smite their foes, and protect the helpless and those who fight at their side.

Almost by definition, the life of a Paladin is an adventuring life, for every Paladin lives on the front lines of the cosmic struggle against annihilation. Fighters are rare enough among the ranks of a world’s armies, but even fewer people can claim the calling of a Paladin. When they do receive the call, these blessed folk turn from their former occupations and take up arms and magic.

#### Becoming a Paladin... {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:BecomingaPaladin}

##### As a Level 1 Character {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:AsaLevel1Character}

[](#illusionist)\* [Gain all the traits in the](#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:illusionist "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes-continued#illusionist") [Core Paladin Traits table](#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:corepaladintraits "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes-continued#corepaladintraits").

- Gain the Paladin’s level 1 features, which are listed in the [Paladin Features table](#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:paladinfeatures "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes-continued#paladinfeatures").

##### As a Multiclass Character {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:AsaMulticlassCharacter}

- Gain the following traits from the [Core Paladin Traits table](#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:corepaladintraits "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes-continued#corepaladintraits"): Hit Point Die, proficiency with Martial weapons, and training with Light and Medium armor and Shields.
- Gain the Paladin’s level 1 features, which are listed in the [Paladin Features table](#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:paladinfeatures "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes-continued#paladinfeatures"). See the multiclassing rules in [chapter 2](#phb-2024:creating-a-character:Multiclassing "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/creating-a-character#Multiclassing") to determine your available spell slots.

#### Level 1: Lay On Hands {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:Level1LayOnHands}

Your blessed touch can heal wounds. You have a pool of healing power that replenishes when you finish a [**Long Rest**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:longrest "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#longrest"). With that pool, you can restore a total number of Hit Points equal to five times your Paladin level.

As a Bonus Action, you can touch a creature (which could be yourself) and draw power from the pool of healing to restore a number of Hit Points to that creature, up to the maximum amount remaining in the pool.

You can also expend 5 Hit Points from the pool of healing power to remove the [**Poisoned**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:poisonedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#poisonedcondition") condition from the creature; those points don’t also restore Hit Points to the creature.

#### Level 1: Spellcasting {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:Level1Spellcasting}

You have learned to cast spells through prayer and meditation. See [chapter 7](#phb-2024:spells "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/spells") for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Paladin spells, which appear in the [Paladin spell list](#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:paladinspelllist "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes-continued#paladinspelllist") later in the class’s description.

**_Spell Slots._** The [Paladin Features table](#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:paladinfeatures "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes-continued#paladinfeatures") shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a [**Long Rest**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:longrest "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#longrest").

**_Prepared Spells of Level 1+_**. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Paladin spells. [**Heroism**](#ref:spell:2619151-heroism "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619151-heroism") and [**Searing Smite**](#ref:spell:2619009-searing-smite "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619009-searing-smite") are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Paladin levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the [Paladin Features table](#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:paladinfeatures "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes-continued#paladinfeatures"). Whenever that number increases, choose additional Paladin spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the Paladin Features table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you’re a level 5 Paladin, your list of prepared spells can include six Paladin spells of level 1 or 2 in any combination.

If another Paladin feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don’t count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Paladin spells for you.

**_Changing Your Prepared Spells._** Whenever you finish a [**Long Rest**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:longrest "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#longrest"), you can replace one spell on your list with another Paladin spell for which you have spell slots.

**_Spellcasting Ability._** Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Paladin spells.

**_Spellcasting Focus._** You can use a [**Holy Symbol**](#ref:equipment:514-holy-symbol "https://www.dndbeyond.com/equipment/514-holy-symbol") as a Spellcasting Focus for your Paladin spells.

#### Level 1: Weapon Mastery {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:Level1WeaponMastery}

Your training with weapons allows you to use the [mastery properties](#phb-2024:equipment:masteryproperties "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/equipment#masteryproperties") of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as Longswords and Javelins.

Whenever you finish a [**Long Rest**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:longrest "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#longrest"), you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the mastery properties of Halberds and Flails.

#### Level 2: Fighting Style {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:Level2FightingStyle}

You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice (see [chapter 5](#phb-2024:feats:FightingStyleFeats "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/feats#FightingStyleFeats") for feats). Instead of choosing one of those feats, you can choose the option below.

**_Blessed Warrior._** You learn two Cleric cantrips of your choice (see the Cleric class’s section for a [list of Cleric spells](#phb-2024:character-classes:clericspelllist "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes#clericspelllist")). [**Guidance**](#ref:spell:2618971-guidance "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618971-guidance") and [**Sacred Flame**](#ref:spell:2618967-sacred-flame "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618967-sacred-flame") are recommended. The chosen cantrips count as Paladin spells for you, and Charisma is your spellcasting ability for them. Whenever you gain a Paladin level, you can replace one of these cantrips with another Cleric cantrip.

#### Level 2: Paladin’s Smite {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:Level2PaladinsSmite}

You always have the [**Divine Smite**](#ref:spell:2618833-divine-smite "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618833-divine-smite") spell prepared. In addition, you can cast it without expending a spell slot, but you must finish a [**Long Rest**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:longrest "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#longrest") before you can cast it in this way again.

#### Level 3: Channel Divinity {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:Level3ChannelDivinity}

You can channel divine energy directly from the Outer Planes, using it to fuel magical effects. You start with one such effect: Divine Sense, which is described below. Other Paladin features give additional Channel Divinity effect options. Each time you use this class’s Channel Divinity, you choose which effect from this class to create.

You can use this class’s Channel Divinity twice. You regain one of its expended uses when you finish a [**Short Rest**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:shortrest "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#shortrest"), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a [**Long Rest**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:longrest "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#longrest"). You gain an additional use when you reach Paladin level 11.

If a Channel Divinity effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals the spell save DC from this class’s Spellcasting feature.

**_Divine Sense._** As a Bonus Action, you can open your awareness to detect Celestials, Fiends, and Undead. For the next 10 minutes or until you have the [**Incapacitated**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:incapacitatedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition") condition, you know the location of any creature of those types within 60 feet of yourself, and you know its creature type. Within the same radius, you also detect the presence of any place or object that has been consecrated or desecrated, as with the [**Hallow**](#ref:spell:2619138-hallow "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619138-hallow") spell.

#### Level 3: Paladin Subclass {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:Level3PaladinSubclass}

You gain a Paladin subclass of your choice. The [Oath of Devotion](#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:oathofdevotion "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes-continued#oathofdevotion"), [Oath of Glory](#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:oathofglory "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes-continued#oathofglory"), [Oath of the Ancients](#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:oathoftheancients "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes-continued#oathoftheancients"), and [Oath of Vengeance](#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:oathofvengeance "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes-continued#oathofvengeance") subclasses are detailed after this class’s description. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Paladin levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass’s features that are of your Paladin level or lower.

> #### Breaking Your Oath {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:paladin:paladinclassfeatures:BreakingYourOath}
>
> A Paladin tries to hold to the highest standards of conduct, but even the most dedicated are fallible. Sometimes a Paladin transgresses their oath.
>
> A Paladin who has broken a vow typically seeks absolution, spending an all-night vigil as a sign of penitence or undertaking a fast. After a rite of forgiveness, the Paladin starts fresh.
>
> If your Paladin unrepentantly violates their oath, talk to your DM. Your Paladin should probably take a more appropriate subclass or even abandon the class and adopt another one.

#### Level 4: Ability Score Improvement {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:Level4AbilityScoreImprovement}

You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see [chapter 5](#phb-2024:feats:abilityscoreimprovement "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/feats#abilityscoreimprovement")) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Paladin levels 8, 12, and 16.

#### Level 5: Extra Attack {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:Level5ExtraAttack}

You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the [**Attack**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:attackaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#attackaction") action on your turn.

#### Level 5: Faithful Steed {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:Level5FaithfulSteed}

You can call on the aid of an otherworldly steed. You always have the [**Find Steed**](#ref:spell:2618879-find-steed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618879-find-steed") spell prepared.

You can also cast the spell once without expending a spell slot, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a [**Long Rest**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:longrest "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#longrest").

[![A Paladin’s dedication to her cause manifests as magical might (Artist: JULIA METZGER)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/04-002.paladin-dedication.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/04-002.paladin-dedication.png)

#### Level 6: Aura of Protection {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:Level6AuraofProtection}

You radiate a protective, unseeable aura in a 10-foot [**Emanation**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:emanationareaofeffect "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#emanationareaofeffect") that originates from you. The aura is inactive while you have the [**Incapacitated**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:incapacitatedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition") condition.

You and your allies in the aura gain a bonus to saving throws equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum bonus of +1).

If another Paladin is present, a creature can benefit from only one Aura of Protection at a time; the creature chooses which aura while in them.

#### Level 9: Abjure Foes {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:Level9AbjureFoes}

As a [**Magic**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:magicaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#magicaction") action, you can expend one use of this class’s Channel Divinity to overwhelm foes with awe. As you present your Holy Symbol or weapon, you can target a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one creature) that you can see within 60 feet of yourself. Each target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the [**Frightened**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:frightenedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition") condition for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. While Frightened in this way, a target can do only one of the following on its turns: move, take an action, or take a Bonus Action.

#### Level 10: Aura of Courage {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:Level10AuraofCourage}

You and your allies have Immunity to the [**Frightened**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:frightenedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition") condition while in your Aura of Protection. If a Frightened ally enters the aura, that condition has no effect on that ally while there.

#### Level 11: Radiant Strikes {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:Level11RadiantStrikes}

Your strikes now carry supernatural power. When you hit a target with an attack roll using a Melee weapon or an [**Unarmed Strike**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:unarmedstrike "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#unarmedstrike"), the target takes an extra 1d8 Radiant damage.

#### Level 14: Restoring Touch {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:Level14RestoringTouch}

When you use Lay On Hands on a creature, you can also remove one or more of the following conditions from the creature: [**Blinded**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:blindedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#blindedcondition"), [**Charmed**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:charmedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#charmedcondition"), [**Deafened**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:deafenedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#deafenedcondition"), [**Frightened**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:frightenedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition"), [**Paralyzed**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:paralyzedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#paralyzedcondition"), or [**Stunned**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:stunnedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#stunnedcondition"). You must expend 5 Hit Points from the healing pool of Lay On Hands for each of these conditions you remove; those points don’t also restore Hit Points to the creature.

#### Level 18: Aura Expansion {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:Level18AuraExpansion}

Your Aura of Protection is now a 30-foot [**Emanation**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:emanationareaofeffect "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#emanationareaofeffect").

#### Level 19: Epic Boon {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:Level19EpicBoon}

You gain an Epic Boon feat (see [chapter 5](#phb-2024:feats:EpicBoonFeats "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/feats#EpicBoonFeats")) or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. [Boon of Truesight](#phb-2024:feats:boonofsensetruesightsense "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/feats#boonofsensetruesightsense") is recommended.

### Paladin Subclasses {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:PaladinSubclasses}

A Paladin subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Paladin levels, as specified in the subclass. This section presents the [Oath of Devotion](#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:oathofdevotion "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes-continued#oathofdevotion"), [Oath of Glory](#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:oathofglory "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes-continued#oathofglory"), [Oath of the Ancients](#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:oathoftheancients "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes-continued#oathoftheancients"), and [Oath of Vengeance](#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:oathofvengeance "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/character-classes-continued#oathofvengeance") subclasses.

Each of these subclasses represents a body of oaths that a Paladin begins taking upon joining the class. The final oath, taken at level 3, is the culmination of a Paladin’s training. Some characters with this class don’t consider themselves true Paladins until they’ve reached level 3 and made this oath. For others, the swearing of the oath is a formality, an official stamp on what was already in their hearts.

#### Oath of Devotion {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:OathofDevotion}

_Uphold the Ideals of Justice and Order_

The Oath of Devotion binds Paladins to the ideals of justice and order. These Paladins meet the archetype of the knight in shining armor. They hold themselves to the highest standards of conduct, and some—for better or worse—hold the rest of the world to the same standards.

Many who swear this oath are devoted to gods of law and good and use their gods’ tenets as the measure of personal devotion. Others hold angels as their ideals and incorporate images of angelic wings into their helmets or coats of arms.

These paladins share the following tenets:

- Let your word be your promise.
- Protect the weak and never fear to act.
- Let your honorable deeds be an example.

##### Level 3: Oath of Devotion Spells {#phb-2024:character-classes-continued:Level3OathofDevotionSpells}

The magic of your oath ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of Devotion Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

[![Oath of Devotion Subclass (Artist: KATERINA LADON)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/04-003.oath-of-devotion.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/04-003.oath-of-devotion.png)
