Armor training allows you to use armor of a certain category without the following drawbacks. If you wear Light, Medium, or Heavy armor and lack training with it, you have Disadvantage on any [D20 Test](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:d20test "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#d20test") that involves Strength or Dexterity, and you can’t cast spells. If you use a Shield and lack training with it, you don’t gain its AC bonus. _See also_ “[Disadvantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:disadvantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#disadvantage")” and chapter 6 (“[Armor](#phb-2024:equipment:Armor "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/equipment#Armor")”).

---

### Attack [Action] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:AttackAction}

When you take the Attack action, you can make one attack roll with a weapon or an [Unarmed Strike](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:unarmedstrike "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#unarmedstrike").

**_Equipping and Unequipping Weapons._** You can either equip or unequip one weapon when you make an attack as part of this action. You do so either before or after the attack. If you equip a weapon before an attack, you don’t need to use it for that attack. Equipping a weapon includes drawing it from a sheath or picking it up. Unequipping a weapon includes sheathing, stowing, or dropping it.

**_Moving between Attacks._** If you move on your turn and have a feature, such as Extra Attack, that gives you more than one attack as part of the Attack action, you can use some or all of that movement to move between those attacks.

---

### Attack Roll {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:AttackRoll}

An attack roll is a [D20 Test](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:d20test "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#d20test") that represents making an attack with a weapon, an [Unarmed Strike](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:unarmedstrike "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#unarmedstrike"), or a spell. _See also_ chapter 1 (“[D20 Tests](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:attackrolls "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#attackrolls")”).

---

### Attitude {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Attitude}

A monster has a starting attitude toward a player character: Friendly, Hostile, or Indifferent. _See also_ “[Friendly](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:friendlyattitude "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#friendlyattitude"),” “[Hostile](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:hostileattitude "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#hostileattitude"),” “[Indifferent](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:indifferentattitude "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#indifferentattitude"),” and “[Influence](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:influenceaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#influenceaction").”

---

### Attunement {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Attunement}

Some magic items require a creature to form a bond—called Attunement—with them before the creature can use an item’s magical properties. A creature can have Attunement with no more than three magic items at a time. _See also_ chapter 6 (“[Magic Items](#phb-2024:equipment:attunement "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/equipment#attunement")”).

---

### Blinded [Condition] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:BlindedCondition}

While you have the Blinded condition, you experience the following effects.

**_Can’t See._** You can’t see and automatically fail any ability check that requires sight.

**_Attacks Affected._** Attack rolls against you have [Advantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:advantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#advantage"), and your attack rolls have [Disadvantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:disadvantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#disadvantage").

---

### Blindsight {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Blindsight}

If you have Blindsight, you can see within a specific range without relying on physical sight. Within that range, you can see anything that isn’t behind [**Total Cover**](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/basic-rules/combat#cover) even if you have the [Blinded](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:blindedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#blindedcondition") condition or are in [Darkness](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:darkness "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#darkness"). Moreover, in that range, you can see something that has the [Invisible](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:invisiblecondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#invisiblecondition") condition.

---

### Bloodied {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Bloodied}

A creature is Bloodied while it has half its [Hit Points](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:hitpoints "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#hitpoints") or fewer remaining.

---

### Bonus Action {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:BonusAction}

A Bonus Action is a special action that you can take on the same turn that you take an action. You can’t take more than one Bonus Action on a turn, and you have a Bonus Action to take only if a rule explicitly says so. _See also_ chapter 1 (“[Actions](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:bonusactions "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#bonusactions")”).

---

### Breaking Objects {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:BreakingObjects}

Objects can be harmed by attacks and by some spells, using the rules below. If an object is exceedingly fragile, the DM may allow a creature to break it automatically with the [Attack](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:attackaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#attackaction") or [Utilize](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:utilizeaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#utilizeaction") action.

**_Armor Class._** The Object Armor Class table suggests ACs for various substances.

**Object Armor Class**

| AC  | Substance           |
| --- | ------------------- |
| 11  | Cloth, paper, rope  |
| 13  | Crystal, glass, ice |
| 15  | Wood                |
| 17  | Stone               |
| 19  | Iron, steel         |
| 21  | Mithral             |
| 23  | Adamantine          |

**_Hit Points._** An object is destroyed when it has 0 [Hit Points](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:hitpoints "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#hitpoints"). The Object Hit Points table suggests Hit Points for fragile and resilient objects that are Large or smaller. To track Hit Points for a Huge or Gargantuan object, divide it into Large or smaller sections, and track each section’s Hit Points separately. The DM determines whether destroying part of an object causes the whole thing to collapse.

**Object Hit Points**

| Size                        | Fragile  | Resilient |
| --------------------------- | -------- | --------- |
| Tiny (bottle, lock)         | 2 (1d4)  | 5 (2d4)   |
| Small (chest, lute)         | 3 (1d6)  | 10 (3d6)  |
| Medium (barrel, chandelier) | 4 (1d8)  | 18 (4d8)  |
| Large (cart, dining table)  | 5 (1d10) | 27 (5d10) |

**_Damage Types and Objects._** Objects have [Immunity](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:immunity "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#immunity") to Poison and Psychic damage. The DM might decide that some damage types are more or less effective against an object. For example, Bludgeoning damage works well for smashing things but not for cutting. Paper or cloth objects might have Vulnerability to Fire damage.

**_Damage Threshold._** Big objects, such as castle walls, often have extra resilience represented by a damage threshold. _See also_ “[Damage Threshold](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:damagethreshold "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#damagethreshold").”

**_No Ability Scores._** An object lacks ability scores unless a rule assigns scores to the object. Without ability scores, an object can’t make ability checks, and it fails all saving throws.

---

### Bright Light {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:BrightLight}

Bright Light is normal illumination. _See also_ chapter 1 (“[Exploration](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:light "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#light")”).

---

### Burning [Hazard] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:BurningHazard}

A burning creature or object takes 1d4 Fire damage at the start of each of its turns. As an action, you can extinguish fire on yourself by giving yourself the [Prone](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:pronecondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#pronecondition") condition and rolling on the ground. The fire also goes out if it is doused, submerged, or suffocated.

---

### Burrow Speed {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:BurrowSpeed}

A creature that has a Burrow Speed can use that speed to move through sand, earth, mud, or ice. The creature can’t burrow through solid rock unless the creature has a trait that allows it to do so. _See also_ “[Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:speed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#speed").”

---

### Campaign {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Campaign}

A campaign is a series of adventures. _See also_ “[Adventure](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:adventure "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#adventure").”

---

### Cantrip {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Cantrip}

A cantrip is a level 0 spell, which is cast without a spell slot. _See also_ [chapter 7](#phb-2024:spells "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/spells").

---

### Carrying Capacity {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:CarryingCapacity}

Your size and Strength score determine the maximum weight in pounds that you can carry, as shown in the Carrying Capacity table. The table also shows the maximum weight you can drag, lift, or push.

While dragging, lifting, or pushing weight in excess of the maximum weight you can carry, your [Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:speed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#speed") can be no more than 5 feet.

**Carrying Capacity**

| Creature Size | Carry          | Drag/Lift/Push |
| ------------- | -------------- | -------------- |
| Tiny          | Str. × 7.5 lb. | Str. × 15 lb.  |
| Small/Medium  | Str. × 15 lb.  | Str. × 30 lb.  |
| Large         | Str. × 30 lb.  | Str. × 60 lb.  |
| Huge          | Str. × 60 lb.  | Str. × 120 lb. |
| Gargantuan    | Str. × 120 lb. | Str. × 240 lb. |

---

### Challenge Rating {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:ChallengeRating}

Challenge Rating (CR) summarizes the threat a monster poses to a group of four player characters. Compare a monster’s CR to the characters’ level. If the CR is higher, the monster is likely a danger. If the CR is lower, the monster likely poses little threat. But circumstances and the number of player characters can significantly alter how threatening a monster is in actual play. The [Dungeon Master’s Guide](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024) provides guidance to the DM on using CR while planning potential combat encounters. _See also_ “[Stat Block](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:statblock "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#statblock").”

---

### Character Sheet {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:CharacterSheet}

A character sheet is a paper or digital record that you use to track your character’s information. _See also_ [chapter 2](#phb-2024:creating-a-character:chooseacharactersheet "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/creating-a-character#chooseacharactersheet").

---

### Charmed [Condition] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:CharmedCondition}

While you have the Charmed condition, you experience the following effects.

**_Can’t Harm the Charmer._** You can’t attack the charmer or target the charmer with damaging abilities or magical effects.

**_Social Advantage._** The charmer has [Advantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:advantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#advantage") on any ability check to interact with you socially.

---

### Climbing {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Climbing}

While you’re climbing, each foot of movement costs 1 extra foot (2 extra feet in [Difficult Terrain](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:difficultterrain "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#difficultterrain")). You ignore this extra cost if you have a [Climb Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:climbspeed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#climbspeed") and use it to climb.

At the DM’s option, climbing a slippery surface or one with few handholds might require a successful DC 15 Strength ([**Athletics**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills")) check.

---

### Climb Speed {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:ClimbSpeed}

A Climb Speed can be used in place of Speed to traverse a vertical surface without expending the extra movement normally associated with climbing. _See also_ “[Climbing](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:climbing "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#climbing")” and “[Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:speed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#speed").”

---

### Concentration {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Concentration}

Some spells and other effects require Concentration to remain active, as specified in their descriptions. If the effect’s creator loses Concentration, the effect ends. If the effect has a maximum duration, the effect’s description specifies how long the creator can concentrate on it: up to 1 minute, 1 hour, or some other duration. The creator can end Concentration at any time (no action required). The following factors break Concentration.

**_Another Concentration Effect._** You lose Concentration on an effect the moment you start casting a spell that requires Concentration or activate another effect that requires Concentration.

**_Damage._** If you take damage, you must succeed on a Constitution saving throw to maintain Concentration. The DC equals 10 or half the damage taken (round down), whichever number is higher, up to a maximum DC of 30.

**_Incapacitated or Dead._** Your Concentration ends if you have the [Incapacitated](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:incapacitatedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition") condition or you die.

---

### Condition {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Condition}

A condition is a temporary game state. The definition of a condition says how it affects its recipient, and various rules define how to end a condition. This glossary defines these conditions:

[Blinded](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:blindedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#blindedcondition")

[Charmed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:charmedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#charmedcondition")

[Deafened](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:deafenedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#deafenedcondition")

[Exhaustion](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:exhaustioncondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#exhaustioncondition")

[Frightened](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:frightenedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#frightenedcondition")

[Grappled](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:grappledcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#grappledcondition")

[Incapacitated](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:incapacitatedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition")

[Invisible](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:invisiblecondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#invisiblecondition")

[Paralyzed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:paralyzedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#paralyzedcondition")

[Petrified](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:petrifiedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#petrifiedcondition")

[Poisoned](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:poisonedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#poisonedcondition")

[Prone](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:pronecondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#pronecondition")

[Restrained](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:restrainedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#restrainedcondition")

[Stunned](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:stunnedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#stunnedcondition")

[Unconscious](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:unconsciouscondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#unconsciouscondition")

A condition doesn’t stack with itself; a recipient either has a condition or doesn’t. The Exhaustion condition is an exception to that rule. _See also_ chapter 1 (“[Conditions](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:Conditions "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#Conditions")”).

---

### Cone [Area of Effect] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:ConeAreaofEffect}

A Cone is an [area of effect](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:areaofeffect "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#areaofeffect") that extends in straight lines from a point of origin in a direction its creator chooses. A Cone’s width at any point along its length is equal to that point’s distance from the point of origin. For example, a Cone is 15 feet wide at a point along its length that is 15 feet from the point of origin. The effect that creates a Cone specifies its maximum length.

A Cone’s point of origin isn’t included in the area of effect unless its creator decides otherwise.

---

### Cover {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Cover}

Cover provides a degree of protection to a target behind it. There are three degrees of cover, each of which provides a different benefit to a target: [**Half Cover**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:cover "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#cover") (+2 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws), [**Three-Quarters Cover**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:cover "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#cover") (+5 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws), and [**Total Cover**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:cover "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#cover") (can’t be targeted directly). If behind more than one degree of cover, a target benefits only from the most protective degree. _See also_ chapter 1 (“[Combat](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:cover "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#cover")”).

---

### Crawling {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Crawling}

While you’re crawling, each foot of movement costs 1 extra foot (2 extra feet in [Difficult Terrain](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:difficultterrain "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#difficultterrain")). _See also_ “[Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:speed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#speed").”

---

### Creature {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Creature}

Any being in the game, including a player’s character, is a creature. _See also_ “[Creature Type](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:creaturetype "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#creaturetype").”

---

### Creature Type {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:CreatureType}

Every creature, including every player character, has a tag in the rules that identifies the type of creature it is. Most player characters are of the Humanoid type. These are the game’s creature types:

Aberration

Beast

Celestial

Construct

Dragon

Elemental

Fey

Fiend

Giant

Humanoid

Monstrosity

Ooze

Plant

Undead

The types don’t have rules themselves, but some rules in the game affect creatures of certain types in different ways.

---

### Critical Hit {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:CriticalHit}

If you roll a 20 on the d20 for an attack roll, you score a Critical Hit, and the attack hits regardless of any modifiers or the target’s AC. A Critical Hit lets you roll extra dice for the attack’s damage against the target. Roll all of the attack’s damage dice twice and add them together. Then add any relevant modifiers. _See also_ chapter 1 (“[Damage and Healing](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:criticalhits "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#criticalhits")”).

---

### Cube [Area of Effect] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:CubeAreaofEffect}

A Cube is an [area of effect](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:areaofeffect "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#areaofeffect") that extends in straight lines from a point of origin located anywhere on a face of the Cube. The effect that creates a Cube specifies its size, which is the length of each side.

A Cube’s point of origin isn’t included in the area of effect unless its creator decides otherwise.

---

### Curses {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Curses}

Some game effects curse a creature or an object. The effect that confers a curse defines what the curse does. Curses can be removed by the [**Remove Curse**](#ref:spell:2618943-remove-curse "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618943-remove-curse") and [**Greater Restoration**](#ref:spell:2618961-greater-restoration "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618961-greater-restoration") spells or other magic that explicitly ends curses.

---

### Cylinder [Area of Effect] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:CylinderAreaofEffect}

A Cylinder is an [area of effect](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:areaofeffect "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#areaofeffect") that extends in straight lines from a point of origin located at the center of the circular top or bottom of the Cylinder. The effect that creates a Cylinder specifies the radius of the Cylinder’s base and the Cylinder’s height.

A Cylinder’s point of origin is included in the area of effect.

[![(Artist: NOOR RAHMAN)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/12-002.planescape-border.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/12-002.planescape-border.png)

---

### D20 Test {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:D20Test}

D20 Tests encompass the three main d20 rolls of the game: [ability checks](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:abilitycheck "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#abilitycheck"), [attack rolls](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:attackroll "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#attackroll"), and [saving throws](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:savingthrow "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#savingthrow"). If something in the game affects D20 Tests, it affects all three of these rolls. The DM determines whether a D20 Test is warranted in a given circumstance. _See also_ chapter 1 (“[D20 Tests](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:D20Tests "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#D20Tests")”).

---

### Damage {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Damage}

Damage represents harm that causes a creature or an object to lose [Hit Points](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:hitpoints "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#hitpoints").

---

### Damage Roll {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:DamageRoll}

A damage roll is a die roll, adjusted by any applicable modifiers, that deals damage to a target. _See also_ chapter 1 (“[Damage and Healing](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:damagerolls "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#damagerolls")”).

---

### Damage Threshold {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:DamageThreshold}

A creature or an object that has a damage threshold has [Immunity](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:immunity "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#immunity") to all damage unless it takes an amount of damage from a single attack or effect equal to or greater than its damage threshold, in which case it takes that entire instance of damage. Any damage that fails to meet or exceed the damage threshold is superficial and doesn’t reduce [Hit Points](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:hitpoints "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#hitpoints"). For example, if an object has a damage threshold of 10, the object takes no damage if 9 damage is dealt to it, since that damage fails to exceed the threshold. If the same object is dealt 11 damage, it takes all of that damage.

---

### Damage Types {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:DamageTypes}

Attacks and other harmful effects deal different types of damage. Damage types have no rules of their own, but other rules, such as [Resistance](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:resistance "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#resistance"), rely on the types. The Damage Types table offers examples to help a DM assign a type to a new effect.

**Damage Types**

| Type        | Examples                             |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Acid        | Corrosive liquids, digestive enzymes |
| Bludgeoning | Blunt objects, constriction, falling |
| Cold        | Freezing water, icy blasts           |
| Fire        | Flames, unbearable heat              |
| Force       | Pure magical energy                  |
| Lightning   | Electricity                          |
| Necrotic    | Life-draining energy                 |
| Piercing    | Fangs, puncturing objects            |
| Poison      | Toxic gas, venom                     |
| Psychic     | Mind-rending energy                  |
| Radiant     | Holy energy, searing radiation       |
| Slashing    | Claws, cutting objects               |
| Thunder     | Concussive sound                     |

---

### Darkness {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Darkness}

An area of Darkness is Heavily Obscured. _See also_ “[Heavily Obscured](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:heavilyobscured "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#heavilyobscured")” and chapter 1 (“[Exploration](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:obscuredareas "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#obscuredareas")”).

---

### Darkvision {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Darkvision}

If you have Darkvision, you can see in [Dim Light](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:dimlight "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#dimlight") within a specified range as if it were [Bright Light](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:brightlight "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#brightlight") and in [Darkness](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:darkness "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#darkness") within that range as if it were Dim Light. You discern colors in that Darkness only as shades of gray. _See also_ chapter 1 (“[Exploration](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:specialsenses "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#specialsenses")”).

---

### Dash [Action] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:DashAction}

When you take the Dash action, you gain extra movement for the current turn. The increase equals your Speed after applying any modifiers. With a Speed of 30 feet, for example, you can move up to 60 feet on your turn if you Dash. If your Speed of 30 feet is reduced to 15 feet, you can move up to 30 feet this turn if you Dash.

If you have a special speed, such as a [Fly Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:flyspeed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#flyspeed") or [Swim Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:swimspeed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#swimspeed"), you can use that speed instead of your Speed when you take this action. You choose which speed to use each time you take it. _See also_ “[Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:speed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#speed").”

---

### Dead {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Dead}

A dead creature has no [Hit Points](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:hitpoints "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#hitpoints") and can’t regain them unless it is first revived by magic such as the [**Raise Dead**](#ref:spell:2618922-raise-dead "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618922-raise-dead") or [**Revivify**](#ref:spell:2618956-revivify "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618956-revivify") spell. When such a spell is cast, the spirit knows who is casting it and can refuse. The spirit of a dead creature has left the body and departed for the Outer Planes, and reviving the creature requires calling the spirit back.

If the creature returns to life, the revival effect determines the creature’s current Hit Points. Unless otherwise stated, the creature returns to life with any conditions, magical contagions, or curses that were affecting it at death if the durations of those effects are still ongoing. If the creature died with any [Exhaustion](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:exhaustioncondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#exhaustioncondition") levels, it returns with 1 fewer level. If the creature had [Attunement](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:attunement "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#attunement") to one or more magic items, it is no longer attuned to them.

---

### Deafened [Condition] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:DeafenedCondition}

While you have the Deafened condition, you experience the following effect.

**_Can’t Hear._** You can’t hear and automatically fail any ability check that requires hearing.

---

### Death Saving Throw {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:DeathSavingThrow}

A player character must make a Death Saving Throw (also called a Death Save) if they start their turn with 0 [Hit Points](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:hitpoints "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#hitpoints"). _See also_ chapter 1 (“[Damage and Healing](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:deathsavingthrows "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#deathsavingthrows")”).

---

### Dehydration [Hazard] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:DehydrationHazard}

A creature requires an amount of water per day based on its size, as shown in the Water Needs per Day table. A creature that drinks less than half the required water for a day gains 1 Exhaustion level at the day’s end. Exhaustion caused by dehydration can’t be removed until the creature drinks the full amount of water required for a day. _See also_ “[Exhaustion](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:exhaustioncondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#exhaustioncondition").”

**Water Needs per Day**

| Size       | Water      |
| ---------- | ---------- |
| Tiny       | 1/4 gallon |
| Small      | 1 gallon   |
| Medium     | 1 gallon   |
| Large      | 4 gallons  |
| Huge       | 16 gallons |
| Gargantuan | 64 gallons |

---

### Difficult Terrain {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:DifficultTerrain}

If a space is Difficult Terrain, every foot of movement in that space costs 1 extra foot. For example, moving 5 feet through Difficult Terrain costs 10 feet of movement. Difficult Terrain isn’t cumulative; either a space is Difficult Terrain or it isn’t.

A space is Difficult Terrain if the space contains any of the following or something similar:

- A creature that isn’t Tiny or your ally
- Furniture that is sized for creatures of your size or larger
- Heavy snow, ice, rubble, or undergrowth
- Liquid that’s between shin- and waist-deep
- A narrow opening sized for a creature one size smaller than you
- A slope of 20 degrees or more

---

### Difficulty Class {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:DifficultyClass}

A Difficulty Class (DC) is the target number for an [ability check](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:abilitycheck "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#abilitycheck") or a [saving throw](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:savingthrow "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#savingthrow"). _See also_ chapter 1 (“[D20 Tests](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:D20Tests "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#D20Tests")”).

---

### Dim Light {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:DimLight}

An area with Dim Light is Lightly Obscured. _See also_ “[Lightly Obscured](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:lightlyobscured "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#lightlyobscured")” and chapter 1 (“[Exploration](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:obscuredareas "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#obscuredareas")”).

---

### Disadvantage {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Disadvantage}

If you have Disadvantage on a [D20 Test](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:d20test "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#d20test"), roll two d20s and use the lower roll. A roll can’t be affected by more than one Disadvantage, and [Advantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:advantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#advantage") and Disadvantage on the same roll cancel each other. _See also_ chapter 1 (“[D20 Tests](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:advantagedisadvantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#advantagedisadvantage")”).

---

### Disengage [Action] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:DisengageAction}

If you take the Disengage action, your movement doesn’t provoke [Opportunity Attacks](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:opportunityattacks "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#opportunityattacks") for the rest of the current turn.

---

### Dodge [Action] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:DodgeAction}

If you take the Dodge action, you gain the following benefits: until the start of your next turn, any attack roll made against you has [Disadvantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:disadvantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#disadvantage") if you can see the attacker, and you make Dexterity saving throws with [Advantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:advantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#advantage").

You lose these benefits if you have the [Incapacitated](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:incapacitatedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition") condition or if your [Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:speed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#speed") is 0.

---

### Emanation [Area of Effect] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:EmanationAreaofEffect}

An Emanation is an [area of effect](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:areaofeffect "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#areaofeffect") that extends in straight lines from a creature or an object in all directions. The effect that creates an Emanation specifies the distance it extends.

An Emanation moves with the creature or object that is its origin unless it is an instantaneous or a stationary effect.

An Emanation’s origin (creature or object) isn’t included in the area of effect unless its creator decides otherwise.

---

### Encounter {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Encounter}

An encounter is a scene in an adventure that is part of at least one of the game’s three pillars: social interaction, exploration, or combat. _See also_ chapter 1 (“[Social Interaction](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:SocialInteraction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#SocialInteraction"),” “[Exploration](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:Exploration "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#Exploration"),” and “[Combat](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:Combat "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#Combat")”).

---

### Enemy {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Enemy}

A creature is your enemy if it fights against you in combat, actively works to harm you, or is designated as your enemy by the rules or DM.

---

### Exhaustion [Condition] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:ExhaustionCondition}

While you have the Exhaustion condition, you experience the following effects.

**_Exhaustion Levels._** This condition is cumulative. Each time you receive it, you gain 1 Exhaustion level. You die if your Exhaustion level is 6.

**_D20 Tests Affected._** When you make a [D20 Test](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:d20test "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#d20test"), the roll is reduced by 2 times your Exhaustion level.

**_Speed Reduced._** Your [Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:speed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#speed") is reduced by a number of feet equal to 5 times your Exhaustion level.

**_Removing Exhaustion Levels._** Finishing a [Long Rest](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:longrest "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#longrest") removes 1 of your Exhaustion levels. When your Exhaustion level reaches 0, the condition ends.

---

### Experience Points {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:ExperiencePoints}

As they overcome challenges and complete adventures, characters earn Experience Points (XP), which are awarded by the Dungeon Master. When a character’s XP total crosses certain thresholds, the character’s level increases. The [Dungeon Master’s Guide](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/dmg-2024) provides guidance on awarding XP. _See also_ chapter 2 (“[Level Advancement](#phb-2024:creating-a-character:LevelAdvancement "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/creating-a-character#LevelAdvancement")”).

---

### Expertise {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Expertise}

Expertise is a feature that enhances your use of a skill proficiency. When you make an ability check with a skill proficiency in which you have Expertise, your Proficiency Bonus is doubled for that check unless the bonus is doubled by another feature.

If you gain Expertise, you gain it in one skill in which you have proficiency. You can’t have Expertise in the same skill proficiency more than once.

_See also_ chapter 1 (“[Proficiency](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:Proficiency "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#Proficiency")”).

---

### Falling [Hazard] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:FallingHazard}

A creature that falls takes 1d6 Bludgeoning damage at the end of the fall for every 10 feet it fell, to a maximum of 20d6. When the creature lands, it has the [Prone](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:pronecondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#pronecondition") condition unless it avoids taking any damage from the fall.

A creature that falls into water or another liquid can use its [Reaction](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:reaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#reaction") to make a DC 15 Strength ([**Athletics**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills")) or Dexterity ([**Acrobatics**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills")) check to hit the surface head or feet first. On a successful check, any damage resulting from the fall is halved.

---

### Flying {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Flying}

A variety of effects allow a creature to fly. While flying, you fall if you have the [Incapacitated](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:incapacitatedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition") or [Prone](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:pronecondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#pronecondition") condition or your Fly Speed is reduced to 0. You can stay aloft in those circumstances if you can hover. _See also_ “[Falling](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:fallinghazard "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#fallinghazard")” and “[Fly Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:flyspeed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#flyspeed").”

---

### Fly Speed {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:FlySpeed}

A Fly Speed can be used to travel through the air. While you have a Fly Speed, you can stay aloft until you land, fall, or die. _See also_ “[Flying](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:flying "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#flying")” and “[Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:speed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#speed").”

---

### Friendly [Attitude] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:FriendlyAttitude}

A Friendly creature views you favorably. You have [Advantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:advantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#advantage") on an ability check to influence a Friendly creature. _See also_ “[Influence](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:influenceaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#influenceaction").”

---

### Frightened [Condition] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:FrightenedCondition}

While you have the Frightened condition, you experience the following effects.

**_Ability Checks and Attacks Affected._** You have [Disadvantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:disadvantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#disadvantage") on [ability checks](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:abilitycheck "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#abilitycheck") and [attack rolls](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:attackroll "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#attackroll") while the source of fear is within line of sight.

**_Can’t Approach._** You can’t willingly move closer to the source of fear.

---

### Grappled [Condition] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:GrappledCondition}

While you have the Grappled condition, you experience the following effects.

**_Speed 0._** Your [Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:speed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#speed") is 0 and can’t increase.

**_Attacks Affected._** You have [Disadvantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:disadvantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#disadvantage") on attack rolls against any target other than the grappler.

**_Movable._** The grappler can drag or carry you when it moves, but every foot of movement costs it 1 extra foot unless you are Tiny or two or more sizes smaller than it.

---

### Grappling {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Grappling}

A creature can grapple another creature. Characters typically grapple by using an Unarmed Strike. Many monsters have special attacks that allow them to quickly grapple prey. However a grapple is initiated, it follows these rules. _See also_ “[Unarmed Strike](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:unarmedstrike "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#unarmedstrike")” and “[Grappled](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:grappledcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#grappledcondition").”

**_Grappled Condition._** Successfully grappling a creature gives it the Grappled condition.

**_One Grapple per Hand._** A creature must have a hand free to grapple another creature. Some stat blocks and game effects allow a creature to grapple using a tentacle, a maw, or another body part. Whatever part a grappler uses, it can grapple only one creature at a time with that part, and the grappler can’t use that part to target another creature unless it ends the grapple.

**_Ending a Grapple._** A Grappled creature can use its action to make a Strength ([**Athletics**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills")) or Dexterity ([**Acrobatics**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills")) check against the grapple’s escape DC, ending the condition on itself on a success. The condition also ends if the grappler has the [Incapacitated](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:incapacitatedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition") condition or if the distance between the Grappled target and the grappler exceeds the grapple’s range. In addition, the grappler can release the target at any time (no action required).

---

### Hazard {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Hazard}

A hazard is an environmental danger. _See also_ “[Burning](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:burninghazard "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#burninghazard"),” “[Dehydration](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:dehydrationhazard "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#dehydrationhazard"),” “[Falling](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:fallinghazard "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#fallinghazard"),” “[Malnutrition](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:malnutritionhazard "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#malnutritionhazard"),” and “[Suffocation](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:suffocationhazard "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#suffocationhazard").”

---

### Healing {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Healing}

Healing is how you regain [Hit Points](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:hitpoints "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#hitpoints"). _See also_ chapter 1 (“[Damage and Healing](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:DamageandHealing "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#DamageandHealing")”).

---

### Heavily Obscured {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:HeavilyObscured}

You have the Blinded condition while trying to see something in a Heavily Obscured space. _See also_ “[Blinded](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:blindedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#blindedcondition"),” “[Darkness](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:darkness "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#darkness"),” and chapter 1 (“[Exploration](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:obscuredareas "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#obscuredareas")”).

---

### Help [Action] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:HelpAction}

When you take the Help action, you do one of the following.

**_Assist an Ability Check._** Choose one of your skill or tool proficiencies and one ally who is near enough for you to assist verbally or physically when they make an ability check. That ally has [Advantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:advantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#advantage") on the next ability check they make with the chosen skill or tool. This benefit expires if the ally doesn’t use it before the start of your next turn. The DM has final say on whether your assistance is possible.

**_Assist an Attack Roll._** You momentarily distract an enemy within 5 feet of you, giving Advantage to the next attack roll by one of your allies against that enemy. This benefit expires at the start of your next turn.

---

### Heroic Inspiration {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:HeroicInspiration}

If you (a player character) have Heroic Inspiration, you can expend it to reroll any die immediately after rolling it, and you must use the new roll.

If you gain Heroic Inspiration but already have it, it’s lost unless you give it to a player character who lacks it.

---

### Hide [Action] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:HideAction}

With the Hide action, you try to conceal yourself. To do so, you must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity ([**Stealth**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills")) check while you’re [Heavily Obscured](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:heavilyobscured "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#heavilyobscured") or behind [**Three-Quarters Cover**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:cover "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#cover") or [**Total Cover**](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:cover "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#cover"), and you must be out of any enemy’s line of sight; if you can see a creature, you can discern whether it can see you.

On a successful check, you have the [Invisible](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:invisiblecondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#invisiblecondition") condition while hidden. Make note of your check’s total, which is the DC for a creature to find you with a Wisdom ([**Perception**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills")) check.

You stop being hidden immediately after any of the following occurs: you make a sound louder than a whisper, an enemy finds you, you make an attack roll, or you cast a spell with a Verbal component.

---

### High Jump {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:HighJump}

When you make a High Jump, you leap into the air a number of feet equal to 3 plus your Strength modifier (minimum of 0 feet) if you move at least 10 feet on foot immediately before the jump. When you make a standing High Jump, you can jump only half that distance. Either way, each foot of the jump costs a foot of movement.

You can extend your arms half your height above yourself during the jump. Thus, you can reach a distance equal to the height of the jump plus 1½ times your height.

---

### Hit Point Dice {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:HitPointDice}

Hit Point Dice, or Hit Dice for short, help determine a player character’s Hit Point maximum, as explained in [chapter 2](#phb-2024:creating-a-character "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/creating-a-character"). Most monsters also have Hit Dice. A creature can spend Hit Dice during a Short Rest to regain [Hit Points](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:hitpoints "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#hitpoints"). _See also_ “[Short Rest](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:shortrest "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#shortrest").”

---

### Hit Points {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:HitPoints}

Hit Points (HP) are a measure of how difficult it is to kill or destroy a creature or an object. Damage reduces Hit Points, and healing restores them. You can’t have more Hit Points than your Hit Point maximum, and you can’t have less than 0. _See also_ “[Breaking Objects](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:breakingobjects "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#breakingobjects")” and chapter 1 (“[Damage and Healing](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:hitpoints "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#hitpoints")”).

---

### Hostile [Attitude] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:HostileAttitude}

A Hostile creature views you unfavorably. You have [Disadvantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:disadvantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#disadvantage") on an ability check to influence a Hostile creature. _See also_ “[Influence](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:influenceaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#influenceaction").”

---

### Hover {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Hover}

Some creatures can hover, as noted in their stat blocks, and some spells and other effects grant the ability to hover. Hovering while flying prevents you from falling in certain circumstances. _See also_ “[Flying](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:flying "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#flying").”

---

### Illusions {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Illusions}

Spells and other effects sometimes create magical illusions. Such an effect defines what the illusion does and which senses or mental faculties it deceives.

If an illusion manifests in space, the illusion is insubstantial and weightless, yet it seems to be affected by the environment as if the illusion were real unless the effect that created it specifies otherwise. For example, a visual illusion of a creature casts shadows and reflections, and wind appears to affect the illusory creature. Similarly, an audible illusion echoes in an echoey space.

---

### Immunity {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Immunity}

If you have Immunity to a damage type or a condition, it doesn’t affect you in any way.

---

### Improvised Weapons {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:ImprovisedWeapons}

An improvised weapon is an object wielded as a makeshift weapon, such as broken glass, a table leg, or a frying pan. A Simple or Martial weapon also counts as an improvised weapon if it’s wielded in a way contrary to its design; if you use a Ranged weapon to make a melee attack or throw a Melee weapon that lacks the [**Thrown**](#phb-2024:equipment:thrown "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/equipment#thrown") property, the weapon counts as an improvised weapon. An improvised weapon follows the rules below.

**_Proficiency._** Don’t add your Proficiency Bonus to attack rolls with an improvised weapon.

**_Damage._** On a hit, the weapon deals 1d4 damage of a type the DM thinks is appropriate for the object.

**_Range._** If you throw the weapon, it has a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet.

**_Weapon Equivalents._** If an improvised weapon resembles a Simple or Martial weapon, the DM may say it functions as that weapon and uses that weapon’s rules. For example, the DM could treat a table leg as a Club.

---

### Incapacitated [Condition] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:IncapacitatedCondition}

While you have the Incapacitated condition, you experience the following effects.

**_Inactive._** You can’t take any [action](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:action "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#action"), [Bonus Action](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:bonusaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#bonusaction"), or [Reaction](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:reaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#reaction").

**_No Concentration._** Your [Concentration](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:concentration "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#concentration") is broken.

**_Speechless._** You can’t speak.

**_Surprised._** If you’re Incapacitated when you roll [Initiative](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:initiative "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#initiative"), you have [Disadvantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:disadvantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#disadvantage") on the roll.

---

### Indifferent [Attitude] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:IndifferentAttitude}

An Indifferent creature has no desire to help or hinder you. Indifferent is the default attitude of a monster. _See also_ “[Influence](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:influenceaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#influenceaction").”

---

### Influence [Action] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:InfluenceAction}

With the Influence action, you urge a monster to do something. Describe or roleplay how you’re communicating with the monster. Are you trying to deceive, intimidate, amuse, or gently persuade? The DM then determines whether the monster feels willing, unwilling, or hesitant due to your interaction; this determination establishes whether an ability check is necessary, as explained below.

**_Willing._** If your urging aligns with the monster’s desires, no ability check is necessary; the monster fulfills your request in a way it prefers.

**_Unwilling._** If your urging is repugnant to the monster or counter to its alignment, no ability check is necessary; it doesn’t comply.

**_Hesitant._** If you urge the monster to do something that it is hesitant to do, you must make an ability check, which is affected by the monster’s attitude: [Indifferent](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:indifferentattitude "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#indifferentattitude"), [Friendly](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:friendlyattitude "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#friendlyattitude"), or [Hostile](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:hostileattitude "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#hostileattitude"), each of which is defined in this glossary. The Influence Checks table suggests which ability check to make based on how you’re interacting with the monster. The DM chooses the check, which has a default DC equal to 15 or the monster’s Intelligence score, whichever is higher. On a successful check, the monster does as urged. On a failed check, you must wait 24 hours (or a duration set by the DM) before urging it in the same way again.

**Influence Checks**

| Ability Check                                                                                            | Interaction                               |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| Charisma ([**Deception**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills"))     | Deceiving a monster that understands you  |
| Charisma ([**Intimidation**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills"))  | Intimidating a monster                    |
| Charisma ([**Performance**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills"))   | Amusing a monster                         |
| Charisma ([**Persuasion**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills"))    | Persuading a monster that understands you |
| Wisdom ([**Animal Handling**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills")) | Gently coaxing a Beast or Monstrosity     |

---

### Initiative {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Initiative}

Initiative determines the order of turns during combat. The combat rules in chapter 1 explain how to roll Initiative.

Sometimes a DM might have combatants use their Initiative scores instead of rolling Initiative. Your Initiative score equals 10 plus your Dexterity modifier. If you have [Advantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:advantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#advantage") on Initiative rolls, increase your Initiative score by 5. If you have [Disadvantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:disadvantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#disadvantage") on those rolls, decrease that score by 5. _See also_ chapter 1 (“[Combat](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:Combat "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#Combat")”).

---

### Invisible [Condition] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:InvisibleCondition}

While you have the Invisible condition, you experience the following effects.

**_Surprise._** If you’re Invisible when you roll [Initiative](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:initiative "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#initiative"), you have [Advantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:advantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#advantage") on the roll.

**_Concealed._** You aren’t affected by any effect that requires its target to be seen unless the effect’s creator can somehow see you. Any equipment you are wearing or carrying is also concealed.

**_Attacks Affected._** Attack rolls against you have [Disadvantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:disadvantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#disadvantage"), and your attack rolls have Advantage. If a creature can somehow see you, you don’t gain this benefit against that creature.

[![(Artist: NOOR RAHMAN)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/12-003.urban-border.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/12-003.urban-border.png)

---

### Jumping {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Jumping}

When you jump, you make either a Long Jump (horizontal) or a High Jump (vertical). _See also_ “[Long Jump](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:longjump "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#longjump")” and “[High Jump](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:highjump "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#highjump").”

---

### Knocking Out a Creature {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:KnockingOutaCreature}

When you would reduce a creature to 0 [Hit Points](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:hitpoints "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#hitpoints") with a melee attack, you can instead reduce the creature to 1 Hit Point. The creature then has the [Unconscious](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:unconsciouscondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#unconsciouscondition") condition and starts a [Short Rest](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:shortrest "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#shortrest").

The creature remains Unconscious until it regains any Hit Points or until someone uses an action to administer first aid to it, which requires a successful DC 10 Wisdom ([**Medicine**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills")) check.

---

### Lightly Obscured {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:LightlyObscured}

You have [Disadvantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:disadvantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#disadvantage") on Wisdom ([**Perception**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills")) checks to see something in a Lightly Obscured space. _See also_ “[Dim Light](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:dimlight "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#dimlight")” and chapter 1 (“[Exploration](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:light "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#light")”).

---

### Line [Area of Effect] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:LineAreaofEffect}

A Line is an [area of effect](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:areaofeffect "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#areaofeffect") that extends from a point of origin in a straight path along its length and covers an area defined by its width. The effect that creates a Line specifies its length and width.

A Line’s point of origin isn’t included in the area of effect unless its creator decides otherwise.

---

### Long Jump {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:LongJump}

When you make a Long Jump, you leap horizontally a number of feet up to your Strength score if you move at least 10 feet immediately before the jump. When you make a standing Long Jump, you can leap only half that distance. Either way, each foot you jump costs a foot of movement.

If you land in [Difficult Terrain](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:difficultterrain "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#difficultterrain"), you must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity ([**Acrobatics**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills")) check or have the [Prone](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:pronecondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#pronecondition") condition.

This Long Jump rule assumes that the height of the jump doesn’t matter, such as a jump across a stream or chasm. At your DM’s option, you must succeed on a DC 10 Strength ([**Athletics**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills")) check to clear a low obstacle (no taller than a quarter of the jump’s distance), such as a hedge or low wall. Otherwise, you hit the obstacle.

---

### Long Rest {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:LongRest}

A Long Rest is a period of extended downtime—at least 8 hours—available to any creature. During a Long Rest, you sleep for at least 6 hours and perform no more than 2 hours of light activity, such as reading, talking, eating, or standing watch.

During sleep, you have the [Unconscious](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:unconsciouscondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#unconsciouscondition") condition. After you finish a Long Rest, you must wait at least 16 hours before starting another one.

**_Benefits of the Rest._** To start a Long Rest, you must have at least 1 Hit Point. When you finish the rest, you gain the following benefits:

**Regain All HP.** You regain all lost [Hit Points](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:hitpoints "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#hitpoints") and all spent Hit Point Dice. If your Hit Point maximum was reduced, it returns to normal.

**Ability Scores Restored.** If any of your ability scores were reduced, they return to normal.

**Exhaustion Reduced.** If you have the [Exhaustion](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:exhaustioncondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#exhaustioncondition") condition, its level decreases by 1.

**Special Feature.** Some features are recharged by a Long Rest. If you have such a feature, it recharges in the way specified in its description.

**_Interrupting the Rest._** A Long Rest is stopped by the following interruptions:

- Rolling [Initiative](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:initiative "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#initiative")
- Casting a spell other than a cantrip
- Taking any damage
- 1 hour of walking or other physical exertion

If you rested at least 1 hour before the interruption, you gain the benefits of a Short Rest. _See also_ “[Short Rest](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:shortrest "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#shortrest").”

You can resume a Long Rest immediately after an interruption. If you do so, the rest requires 1 additional hour per interruption to finish.

---

### Magic [Action] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:MagicAction}

When you take the Magic action, you cast a spell that has a casting time of an action or use a feature or magic item that requires a Magic action to be activated.

If you cast a spell that has a casting time of 1 minute or longer, you must take the Magic action on each turn of that casting, and you must maintain Concentration while you do so. If your Concentration is broken, the spell fails, but you don’t expend a spell slot. _See also_ “[Concentration](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:concentration "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#concentration").”

---

### Magical Effect {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:MagicalEffect}

An effect is magical if it is created by a spell, a magic item, or a phenomenon that a rule labels as magical.

---

### Malnutrition [Hazard] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:MalnutritionHazard}

A creature needs an amount of food per day based on its size, as shown in the Food Needs per Day table. A creature that eats but consumes less than half the required food for a day must succeed on a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or gain 1 Exhaustion level at the day’s end. A creature that eats nothing for 5 days automatically gains 1 Exhaustion level at the end of the fifth day as well as an additional level at the end of each subsequent day without food.

Exhaustion caused by malnutrition can’t be removed until the creature eats the full amount of food required for a day. _See also_ “[Exhaustion](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:exhaustioncondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#exhaustioncondition").”

**Food Needs per Day**

| Size       | Food      |
| ---------- | --------- |
| Tiny       | 1/4 pound |
| Small      | 1 pound   |
| Medium     | 1 pound   |
| Large      | 4 pounds  |
| Huge       | 16 pounds |
| Gargantuan | 64 pounds |

---

### Monster {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Monster}

A monster is a creature controlled by the DM, even if the creature is benevolent. _See also_ “[Creature](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:creature "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#creature")” and “[NPC](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:nonplayercharacter "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#nonplayercharacter").”

---

### Nonplayer Character {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:NonplayerCharacter}

A nonplayer character (NPC) is a monster that has a personal name and a distinct personality. _See also_ “[Monster](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:monster "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#monster").”

---

### Object {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Object}

An object is a nonliving, distinct thing. Composite things, like buildings, comprise more than one object. _See also_ “[Breaking Objects](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:breakingobjects "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#breakingobjects").”

---

### Occupied Space {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:OccupiedSpace}

A space is occupied if a creature is in it or if it is completely filled by objects.

---

### Opportunity Attacks {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:OpportunityAttacks}

You can make an Opportunity Attack when a creature that you can see leaves your reach using its action, its Bonus Action, its [Reaction](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:reaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#reaction"), or one of its speeds. To make the Opportunity Attack, take a Reaction to make one melee attack with a weapon or an [Unarmed Strike](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:unarmedstrike "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#unarmedstrike") against the provoking creature. The attack occurs right before the creature leaves your reach. _See also_ chapter 1 (“[Combat](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:opportunityattacks "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#opportunityattacks")”).

---

### Paralyzed [Condition] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:ParalyzedCondition}

While you have the Paralyzed condition, you experience the following effects.

**_Incapacitated._** You have the [Incapacitated](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:incapacitatedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition") condition.

**_Speed 0._** Your [Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:speed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#speed") is 0 and can’t increase.

**_Saving Throws Affected._** You automatically fail Strength and Dexterity [saving throws](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:savingthrow "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#savingthrow").

**_Attacks Affected._** Attack rolls against you have [Advantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:advantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#advantage").

**_Automatic Critical Hits._** Any attack roll that hits you is a [Critical Hit](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:criticalhit "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#criticalhit") if the attacker is within 5 feet of you.

---

### Passive Perception {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:PassivePerception}

Passive Perception is a score that reflects a creature’s general awareness of its surroundings. The DM uses this score when determining whether a creature notices something without consciously making a Wisdom ([**Perception**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills")) check.

A creature’s Passive Perception equals 10 plus the creature’s Wisdom ([**Perception**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills")) check bonus. If the creature has [Advantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:advantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#advantage") on such checks, increase the score by 5. If the creature has [Disadvantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:disadvantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#disadvantage") on them, decrease the score by 5. For example, a level 1 character with a Wisdom of 15 and proficiency in Perception has a Passive Perception of 14 (10 + 2 + 2). If that character has Advantage on Wisdom ([**Perception**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills")) checks, the score becomes 19.

---

### Per Day {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:PerDay}

If a rule says you can use something a certain number of times per day, that means you must finish a [Long Rest](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:longrest "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#longrest") to use it again after you run out of uses.

---

### Petrified [Condition] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:PetrifiedCondition}

While you have the Petrified condition, you experience the following effects.

**_Turned to Inanimate Substance._** You are transformed, along with any nonmagical objects you are wearing and carrying, into a solid inanimate substance (usually stone). Your weight increases by a factor of ten, and you cease aging.

**_Incapacitated._** You have the [Incapacitated](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:incapacitatedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition") condition.

**_Speed 0._** Your [Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:speed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#speed") is 0 and can’t increase.

**_Attacks Affected._** Attack rolls against you have [Advantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:advantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#advantage").

**_Saving Throws Affected._** You automatically fail Strength and Dexterity [saving throws](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:savingthrow "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#savingthrow").

**_Resist Damage._** You have [Resistance](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:resistance "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#resistance") to all damage.

**_Poison Immunity._** You have [Immunity](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:immunity "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#immunity") to the [Poisoned](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:poisonedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#poisonedcondition") condition.

---

### Player Character {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:PlayerCharacter}

A player character is a character controlled by a player. _See also_ [chapter 2](#phb-2024:creating-a-character "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/creating-a-character").

---

### Poisoned [Condition] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:PoisonedCondition}

While you have the Poisoned condition, you experience the following effect.

**_Ability Checks and Attacks Affected._** You have [Disadvantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:disadvantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#disadvantage") on attack rolls and ability checks.

---

### Possession {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Possession}

Some effects cause a creature to be possessed by another creature or entity. A possessing effect defines how the possession operates. Possession can be prevented by the [**Protection from Evil and Good**](#ref:spell:2618912-protection-from-evil-and-good "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618912-protection-from-evil-and-good") spell and ended by the [**Dispel Evil and Good**](#ref:spell:2619096-dispel-evil-and-good "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2619096-dispel-evil-and-good") spell.

---

### Proficiency {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Proficiency}

If you have proficiency with something, you can add your Proficiency Bonus to any [D20 Test](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:d20test "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#d20test") you make using that thing. A creature might have proficiency in a skill or saving throw or with a weapon or tool. _See also_ chapter 1 (“[Proficiency](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:Proficiency "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#Proficiency")”).

---

### Prone [Condition] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:ProneCondition}

While you have the Prone condition, you experience the following effects.

**_Restricted Movement._** Your only movement options are to crawl or to spend an amount of movement equal to half your [Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:speed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#speed") (round down) to right yourself and thereby end the condition. If your Speed is 0, you can’t right yourself.

**_Attacks Affected._** You have [Disadvantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:disadvantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#disadvantage") on attack rolls. An attack roll against you has [Advantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:advantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#advantage") if the attacker is within 5 feet of you. Otherwise, that attack roll has Disadvantage.

---

### Reach {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Reach}

A creature has a reach of 5 feet unless a rule says otherwise.

---

### Reaction {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Reaction}

A Reaction is a special action taken in response to a trigger defined in the Reaction’s description. You can take a Reaction on another creature’s turn, and if you take it on your turn, you can do so even if you also take an action, a [Bonus Action](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:bonusaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#bonusaction"), or both. Once you take a Reaction, you can’t take another one until the start of your next turn. The Opportunity Attack is a Reaction available to all creatures. _See also_ “[Opportunity Attacks](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:opportunityattacks "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#opportunityattacks")” and chapter 1 (“[Actions](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:reactions "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#reactions")”).

---

### Ready [Action] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:ReadyAction}

You take the Ready action to wait for a particular circumstance before you act. To do so, you take this action on your turn, which lets you act by taking a [Reaction](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:reaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#reaction") before the start of your next turn.

First, you decide what perceivable circumstance will trigger your Reaction. Then, you choose the action you will take in response to that trigger, or you choose to move up to your [Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:speed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#speed") in response to it. Examples include “If the cultist steps on the trapdoor, I’ll pull the lever that opens it,” and “If the zombie steps next to me, I move away.”

When the trigger occurs, you can either take your Reaction right after the trigger finishes or ignore the trigger.

When you Ready a spell, you cast it as normal (expending any resources used to cast it) but hold its energy, which you release with your Reaction when the trigger occurs. To be readied, a spell must have a casting time of an action, and holding on to the spell’s magic requires [Concentration](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:concentration "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#concentration"), which you can maintain up to the start of your next turn. If your Concentration is broken, the spell dissipates without taking effect.

---

### Resistance {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Resistance}

If you have Resistance to a damage type, damage of that type is halved against you (round down). Resistance is applied only once to an instance of damage. _See also_ chapter 1 (“[Damage and Healing](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:resistanceandvulnerability "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#resistanceandvulnerability")”).

---

### Restrained [Condition] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:RestrainedCondition}

While you have the Restrained condition, you experience the following effects.

**_Speed 0._** Your [Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:speed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#speed") is 0 and can’t increase.

**_Attacks Affected._** Attack rolls against you have [Advantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:advantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#advantage"), and your attack rolls have [Disadvantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:disadvantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#disadvantage").

**_Saving Throws Affected._** You have Disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws.

---

### Ritual {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Ritual}
