If you have a spell prepared that has the Ritual tag, you can cast that spell as a Ritual. The Ritual version of a spell takes 10 minutes longer to cast than normal. It also doesn’t expend a spell slot, which means the ritual version of a spell can’t be cast at a higher level. _See also_ [chapter 7](#phb-2024:spells "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/spells").

---

### Round Down {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:RoundDown}

Whenever you divide or multiply a number in the game, round down if you end up with a fraction, even if the fraction is one-half or greater. Some rules make an exception and tell you to round up.

[![(Artist: NOOR RAHMAN)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/12-004.sea-border.png)](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/phb/MKDHZ1nxSXDDLOw2/12-004.sea-border.png)

---

### Save {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Save}

Save is another name for a saving throw. _See also_ “[Saving Throw](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:savingthrow "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#savingthrow").”

---

### Saving Throw {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:SavingThrow}

A saving throw—also called a save—represents an attempt to avoid or resist a threat. You normally make a saving throw only when a rule requires you to do so, but you can decide to fail the save without rolling. The result of a save is detailed in the effect that allowed it. If a target is forced to make a save and lacks the ability score used by it, the target automatically fails. _See also_ chapter 1 (“[D20 Tests](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:savingthrows "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#savingthrows")”).

---

### Search [Action] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:SearchAction}

When you take the Search action, you make a Wisdom check to discern something that isn’t obvious. The Search table suggests which skills are applicable when you take this action, depending on what you’re trying to detect.

**Search**

| Skill                                                                                      | Thing to Detect                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------ |
| [**Insight**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills")    | Creature’s state of mind             |
| [**Medicine**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills")   | Creature’s ailment or cause of death |
| [**Perception**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills") | Concealed creature or object         |
| [**Survival**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills")   | Tracks or food                       |

---

### Shape-Shifting {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:ShapeShifting}

If an effect, such as Wild Shape or the [**Polymorph**](#ref:spell:2618876-polymorph "https://www.dndbeyond.com/spells/2618876-polymorph") spell, lets you shape-shift, its description specifies what happens to you. Unless that description says otherwise, any ongoing effects on you—[conditions](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:condition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#condition"), [spells](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:spell "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#spell"), [curses](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:curses "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#curses"), and the like—carry over from one form to the other. You revert to your true form if you die.

---

### Short Rest {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:ShortRest}

A Short Rest is a 1-hour period of downtime, during which a creature does nothing more strenuous than reading, talking, eating, or standing watch. To start a Short Rest, you must have at least 1 Hit Point.

**_Benefits of the Rest._** When you finish the rest, you gain the following benefits:

**Spend Hit Point Dice.** You can spend one or more of your Hit Point Dice to regain [Hit Points](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:hitpoints "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#hitpoints"). For each Hit Point Die you spend in this way, roll the die and add your Constitution modifier to it. You regain Hit Points equal to the total (minimum of 1 Hit Point). You can decide to spend an additional Hit Point Die after each roll.

**Special Feature.** Some features are recharged by a Short Rest. If you have such a feature, it recharges in the way specified in its description.

**_Interrupting the Rest._** A Short Rest is stopped by the following interruptions:

- Rolling [Initiative](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:initiative "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#initiative")
- Casting a spell other than a cantrip
- Taking any damage

An interrupted Short Rest confers no benefits.

---

### Simultaneous Effects {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:SimultaneousEffects}

If two or more things happen at the same time on a turn, the person at the game table—player or DM—whose turn it is decides the order in which those things happen. For example, if two effects occur at the start of a player character’s turn, the player decides which of the effects happens first.

---

### Size {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Size}

A creature or an object belongs to a size category: Tiny, Small, Medium, Large, Huge, or Gargantuan. A creature’s size determines how much space the creature occupies in combat. An object’s size affects its [Hit Points](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:hitpoints "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#hitpoints"). _See also_ “[Breaking Objects](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:breakingobjects "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#breakingobjects")” and chapter 1 (“[Combat](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:Combat "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#Combat")”).

---

### Skill {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Skill}

A skill is an area of specialization associated with an ability check. If you have [proficiency](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Proficiency "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#Proficiency") in a skill, you can add your Proficiency Bonus when you make an ability check associated with that skill. _See also_ chapter 1 (“[Proficiency](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skillproficiencies "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skillproficiencies")”).

---

### Speed {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Speed}

A creature has a Speed, which is the distance in feet the creature can cover when it moves on its turn. _See also_ “[Climbing](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:climbing "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#climbing"),” “[Crawling](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:crawling "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#crawling"),” “[Flying](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:flying "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#flying"),” “[Jumping](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:jumping "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#jumping"),” “[Swimming](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:swimming "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#swimming")” and chapter 1 (“[Combat](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:movementandposition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#movementandposition")”).

**_Special Speeds._** Some creatures have special speeds, such as a [Burrow Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:burrowspeed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#burrowspeed"), [Climb Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:climbspeed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#climbspeed"), [Fly Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:flyspeed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#flyspeed"), or [Swim Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:swimspeed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#swimspeed"), each of which is defined in this glossary. If you have more than one speed, choose which one to use when you move; you can switch between the speeds during your move. Whenever you switch, subtract the distance already moved from the new speed. The result determines how much farther you can move. If the result is 0 or less, you can’t use the new speed during the current move. For example, if you have a Speed of 30 and a Fly Speed of 40, you could fly 10 feet, walk 10 feet, and leap into the air to fly 20 feet more.

**_Changes to Your Speeds._** If an effect increases or decreases your Speed for a time, any special speed you have increases or decreases by an equal amount for the same duration. For example, if your Speed is reduced to 0 and you have a Climb Speed, your Climb Speed is also reduced to 0. Similarly, if your Speed is halved and you have a Fly Speed, your Fly Speed is also halved.

---

### Spell {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Spell}

A spell is a magical effect that has the characteristics described in [chapter 7](#phb-2024:spells "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/spells").

---

### Spell Attack {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:SpellAttack}

A spell attack is an attack roll made as part of a spell or another magical effect. _See also_ chapter 7 (“[Casting Spells](#phb-2024:spells:CastingSpells "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/spells#CastingSpells")”).

---

### Spellcasting Focus {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:SpellcastingFocus}

A Spellcasting Focus is an object that certain creatures can use in place of a spell’s Material components if those materials aren’t consumed by the spell and don’t have a cost specified. Some classes allow its members to use certain types of Spellcasting Focuses. _See also_ chapter 7 (“[Casting Spells](#phb-2024:spells:CastingSpells "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/spells#CastingSpells")”).

---

### Sphere [Area of Effect] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:SphereAreaofEffect}

A Sphere is an [area of effect](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:areaofeffect "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#areaofeffect") that extends in straight lines from a point of origin outward in all directions. The effect that creates a Sphere specifies the distance it extends as the radius of the Sphere.

A Sphere’s point of origin is included in the Sphere’s area of effect.

---

### Stable {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Stable}

A creature is Stable if it has 0 [Hit Points](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:hitpoints "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#hitpoints") but isn’t required to make [Death Saving Throws](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:deathsavingthrow "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#deathsavingthrow"). _See also_ chapter 1 (“[Damage and Healing](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:stabilizingacharacter "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#stabilizingacharacter")”).

---

### Stat Block {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:StatBlock}

A stat block contains the game statistics of a monster. Each stat block includes the following information presented after the monster’s name.

**_Size._** A monster is Tiny, Small, Medium, Large, Huge, or Gargantuan. _See also_ “[Size](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:size "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#size").”

**_Creature Type._** This entry notes the family of beings a monster belongs to, along with any descriptive tags. _See also_ “[Creature Type](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:creaturetype "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#creaturetype").”

**_Alignment._** An alignment is suggested for the monster, with the DM determining its actual alignment. _See also_ “[Alignment](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:alignment "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#alignment").”

**_AC, Initiative, and HP._** These entries give the monster’s [Armor Class](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:armorclass "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#armorclass"), [Initiative](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:initiative "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#initiative"), and [Hit Points](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:hitpoints "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#hitpoints"), which are detailed in [chapter 1](#phb-2024:playing-the-game "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game"). In parentheses after the Hit Points, the monster’s [Hit Point Dice](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:hitpointdice "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#hitpointdice") are provided, along with the contribution of its Constitution, if any, to its Hit Points. Following the Initiative modifier is an Initiative score. Some creatures that are created by magic lack Hit Dice and Initiative information.

**_Speed._** Here the monster’s Speed is provided, along with any special speeds. _See also_ “[Burrow Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:burrowspeed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#burrowspeed"),” “[Climb Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:climbspeed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#climbspeed"),” “[Fly Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:flyspeed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#flyspeed"),” and “[Swim Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:swimspeed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#swimspeed").”

**_Ability Scores._** A table provides the monster’s [ability scores, modifiers](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:abilityscoreandmodifier "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#abilityscoreandmodifier"), and [saving throw](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:savingthrow "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#savingthrow") modifiers, all of which are detailed in [chapter 1](#phb-2024:playing-the-game "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game").

**_Skills._** This entry lists the monster’s skill [proficiencies](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Proficiency "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#Proficiency"), if any. _See also_ chapter 1 (“[Proficiency](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:Proficiency "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#Proficiency")”).

**_Resistances and Vulnerabilities._** These entries list the monster’s Resistances and Vulnerabilities, if any. _See also_ “[Resistance](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:resistance "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#resistance")” and “[Vulnerability](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:vulnerability "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#vulnerability").”

**_Immunities._** This section lists the monster’s damage and condition Immunities, if any. _See also_ “[Immunity](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:immunity "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#immunity").”

**_Gear._** If the monster has any equipment that can be given away or retrieved, it’s listed in this entry.

**_Senses._** This entry lists the monster’s special senses, such as [Darkvision](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:darkvision "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#darkvision"), and its Passive Perception. _See also_ “[Passive Perception](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:passiveperception "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#passiveperception").”

**_Languages._** This entry lists any languages the monster knows.

**_CR._** Challenge Rating summarizes the threat a monster poses and is detailed in the [Monster Manual](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/mm-2024). The Experience Points characters receive for defeating a monster and its Proficiency Bonus follow. Some creatures that are created by magic have no CR. _See also_ “[Challenge Rating](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:challengerating "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#challengerating")” and “[Experience Points](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:experiencepoints "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#experiencepoints").”

**_Traits._** The monster’s traits, if any, are features that are active at all times or in certain situations.

**_Actions._** The monster can take these actions in addition to those detailed in this glossary. _See also_ chapter 1 (“[Actions](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:Actions "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#Actions")”).

**_Bonus Actions._** If the monster has [Bonus Action](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:bonusaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#bonusaction") options, they are listed in this section.

**_Reactions._** If the monster can take special [Reactions](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:reaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#reaction"), those are listed in this section.

**_Attack Notation._** The entry for a monster’s attack starts by identifying whether the attack is a melee or a ranged attack and then provides the attack roll’s bonus, its reach or range, and what happens on a hit. An attack is against one target unless its entry says otherwise.

**_Saving Throw Effect Notation._** If an effect forces a saving throw, the effect’s entry starts by identifying the kind of saving throw required and then provides the save’s DC, a description of which creatures must make the save, and what happens on a failed or a successful save.

**_Damage Notation._** A stat block usually provides both a static number and a die expression for each instance of damage. For example, an attack might deal 4 (1d4 + 2) damage on a hit. The DM determines whether you use the static number or the die expression in parentheses; you don’t use both.

---

### Study [Action] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:StudyAction}

When you take the Study action, you make an Intelligence check to study your memory, a book, a clue, or another source of knowledge and call to mind an important piece of information about it.

The Areas of Knowledge table suggests which skills are applicable to various areas of knowledge.

**Areas of Knowledge**

| Skill                                                                                         | Areas                                                                                                                                                               |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [**Arcana**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills")        | Spells, magic items, eldritch symbols, magical traditions, planes of existence, and certain creatures (Aberrations, Constructs, Elementals, Fey, and Monstrosities) |
| [**History**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills")       | Historic events and people, ancient civilizations, wars, and certain creatures (Giants and Humanoids)                                                               |
| [**Investigation**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills") | Traps, ciphers, riddles, and gadgetry                                                                                                                               |
| [**Nature**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills")        | Terrain, flora, weather, and certain creatures (Beasts, Dragons, Oozes, and Plants)                                                                                 |
| [**Religion**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills")      | Deities, religious hierarchies and rites, holy symbols, cults, and certain creatures (Celestials, Fiends, and Undead)                                               |

---

### Stunned [Condition] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:StunnedCondition}

While you have the Stunned condition, you experience the following effects.

**_Incapacitated._** You have the [Incapacitated](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:incapacitatedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition") condition.

**_Saving Throws Affected._** You automatically fail Strength and Dexterity [saving throws](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:savingthrow "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#savingthrow").

**_Attacks Affected._** Attack rolls against you have [Advantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:advantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#advantage").

---

### Suffocation [Hazard] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:SuffocationHazard}

A creature can hold its breath for a number of minutes equal to 1 plus its Constitution modifier (minimum of 30 seconds) before suffocation begins. When a creature runs out of breath or is choking, it gains 1 [Exhaustion](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:exhaustioncondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#exhaustioncondition") level at the end of each of its turns. When a creature can breathe again, it removes all levels of Exhaustion it gained from suffocating.

---

### Surprise {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Surprise}

If a creature is caught unawares by the start of combat, that creature is surprised, which causes it to have [Disadvantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:disadvantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#disadvantage") on its [Initiative](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:initiative "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#initiative") roll. _See also_ chapter 1 (“[Combat](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:Combat "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#Combat")”).

---

### Swimming {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Swimming}

While you’re swimming, each foot of movement costs 1 extra foot (2 extra feet in [Difficult Terrain](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:difficultterrain "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#difficultterrain")). You ignore this extra cost if you have a [Swim Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:swimspeed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#swimspeed") and use it to swim. At the DM’s option, moving any distance in rough water might require a successful DC 15 Strength ([**Athletics**](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:skills "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#skills")) check.

---

### Swim Speed {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:SwimSpeed}

A Swim Speed can be used to swim without expending the extra movement normally associated with swimming. _See also_ “[Swimming](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:swimming "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#swimming")” and “[Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:speed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#speed").”

---

### Target {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Target}

A target is the creature or object targeted by an attack roll, forced to make a [saving throw](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:savingthrow "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#savingthrow") by an effect, or selected to receive the effects of a spell or another phenomenon.

---

### Telepathy {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Telepathy}

Telepathy is a magical ability that allows a creature to communicate mentally with another creature within a specified range. Unless a rule states otherwise, the contacted creature doesn’t need to share a language with the telepath to understand this communication, but the contacted creature must be able to understand at least one language or be telepathic itself to understand.

A telepath doesn’t need to see a contacted creature, and the telepath can start or end the telepathic contact at any time (no action required). Telepathic contact can’t be initiated and is immediately broken if either the telepath or the other creature has the [Incapacitated](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:incapacitatedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition") condition. Telepathic contact is also broken if the contacted creature is no longer within the telepathy’s range or if the telepath contacts a different creature within range.

A creature without telepathy can receive telepathic messages but can’t initiate a telepathic conversation. Once a telepathic conversation starts, the non-telepath can communicate mentally to the telepath until the telepathic connection ends.

---

### Teleportation {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Teleportation}

Teleportation is a special kind of magical transportation. If you teleport, you disappear and reappear elsewhere instantly, without moving through the intervening space. This transportation doesn’t expend movement unless a rule tells you otherwise, and teleportation never provokes [Opportunity Attacks](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:opportunityattacks "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#opportunityattacks").

When you teleport, all the equipment you’re wearing and carrying teleports with you. If you’re touching another creature when you teleport, that creature doesn’t teleport with you unless the teleportation effect says otherwise.

If the destination space of your teleportation is occupied by another creature or blocked by a solid obstacle, you instead appear in the nearest unoccupied space of your choice.

The description of a teleportation effect tells you if you must see the teleportation’s destination.

---

### Temporary Hit Points {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:TemporaryHitPoints}

Temporary Hit Points are granted by certain effects and act as a buffer against losing real [Hit Points](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:hitpoints "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#hitpoints"). _See also_ chapter 1 (“[Damage and Healing](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:temporaryhitpoints "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#temporaryhitpoints")”).

---

### Tremorsense {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Tremorsense}

A creature with Tremorsense can pinpoint the location of creatures and moving objects within a specific range, provided that the creature with Tremorsense and anything it is detecting are both in contact with the same surface (such as the ground, a wall, or a ceiling) or the same liquid.

Tremorsense can’t detect creatures or objects in the air, and it doesn’t count as a form of sight.

---

### Truesight {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Truesight}

If you have Truesight, your vision is enhanced within a specified range. Within that range, your vision pierces through the following:

**Darkness.** You can see in normal and magical [Darkness](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:darkness "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#darkness").

**Invisibility.** You see creatures and objects that have the [Invisible](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:invisiblecondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#invisiblecondition") condition.

**Visual Illusions.** Visual illusions appear transparent to you, and you automatically succeed on saving throws against them.

**Transformations.** You discern the true form of any creature or object you see that has been transformed by magic.

**Ethereal Plane.** You see into the Ethereal Plane. _See also_ appendix A (“[Transitive Planes](#phb-2024:the-multiverse:TransitivePlanes "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/the-multiverse#TransitivePlanes")”).

---

### Unarmed Strike {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:UnarmedStrike}

Instead of using a weapon to make a melee attack, you can use a punch, kick, headbutt, or similar forceful blow. In game terms, this is an Unarmed Strike—a melee attack that involves you using your body to damage, grapple, or shove a target within 5 feet of you.

Whenever you use your Unarmed Strike, choose one of the following options for its effect.

**_Damage._** You make an [attack roll](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:attackroll "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#attackroll") against the target. Your bonus to the roll equals your Strength modifier plus your Proficiency Bonus. On a hit, the target takes Bludgeoning damage equal to 1 plus your Strength modifier.

**_Grapple._** The target must succeed on a Strength or Dexterity saving throw (it chooses which), or it has the [Grappled](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:grappledcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#grappledcondition") condition. The DC for the saving throw and any escape attempts equals 8 plus your Strength modifier and Proficiency Bonus. This grapple is possible only if the target is no more than one size larger than you and if you have a hand free to grab it.

**_Shove._** The target must succeed on a Strength or Dexterity saving throw (it chooses which), or you either push it 5 feet away or cause it to have the [Prone](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:pronecondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#pronecondition") condition. The DC for the saving throw equals 8 plus your Strength modifier and Proficiency Bonus. This shove is possible only if the target is no more than one size larger than you.

_See also_ “[Grappling](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:grappling "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#grappling").”

---

### Unconscious [Condition] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:UnconsciousCondition}

While you have the Unconscious condition, you experience the following effects.

**_Inert._** You have the [Incapacitated](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:incapacitatedcondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#incapacitatedcondition") and [Prone](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:pronecondition "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#pronecondition") conditions, and you drop whatever you’re holding. When this condition ends, you remain Prone.

**_Speed 0._** Your [Speed](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:speed "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#speed") is 0 and can’t increase.

**_Attacks Affected._** [Attack rolls](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:attackroll "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#attackroll") against you have [Advantage](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:advantage "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#advantage").

**_Saving Throws Affected._** You automatically fail Strength and Dexterity [saving throws](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:savingthrow "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#savingthrow").

**_Automatic Critical Hits._** Any attack roll that hits you is a [Critical Hit](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:criticalhit "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#criticalhit") if the attacker is within 5 feet of you.

**_Unaware._** You’re unaware of your surroundings.

---

### Unoccupied Space {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:UnoccupiedSpace}

A space is unoccupied if no creatures are in it and it isn’t completely filled by objects.

---

### Utilize [Action] {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:UtilizeAction}

You normally interact with an object while doing something else, such as when you draw a sword as part of the [Attack](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:attackaction "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#attackaction") action. When an object requires an action for its use, you take the Utilize action.

---

### Vulnerability {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Vulnerability}

If you have Vulnerability to a damage type, damage of that type is doubled against you. Vulnerability is applied only once to an instance of damage. _See also_ chapter 1 (“[Damage and Healing](#phb-2024:playing-the-game:resistanceandvulnerability "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/playing-the-game#resistanceandvulnerability")”).

---

### Weapon {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:Weapon}

A weapon is an object that is in the Simple or Martial weapon category. _See also_ chapter 6 (“[Weapons](#phb-2024:equipment:Weapons "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/equipment#Weapons")”).

---

### Weapon Attack {#phb-2024:rules-glossary:WeaponAttack}

A weapon attack is an attack roll made with a weapon. _See also_ “[Weapon](#phb-2024:rules-glossary:weapon "https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/phb-2024/rules-glossary#weapon").”

</CHAPTER>
